title.zh: 卷99 私署凉州牧張實 鮮卑乞伏國仁 鮮卑秃發烏孤 私署凉王李暠 盧水胡沮渠蒙遜
title.en: Volume 99: Governor Mu Zhangshi of Liangzhou, Qifu Guoren of the Xianbei, Tufa Wugu of the Xianbei, Governor Liangwang Ligao, Juqu Mengxun of the Lushui People
title.raw: 卷99 私署凉州牧張實 鮮卑乞伏國仁 鮮卑秃發烏孤 私署凉王李暠 盧水胡沮渠蒙遜 Volume 99: Governor Mu Zhangshi of Liangzhou, Qifu Guoren of the Xianbei, Tufa Wugu of the Xianbei, Governor Liangwang Ligao, Juqu Mengxun of the Lushui People

sentences.zh: 私署涼州牧張寔 鮮卑乞伏國仁 鮮卑禿髮烏孤 私署涼王李暠 盧水胡沮渠蒙遜

translations.literal: Self-appointed Governor of Liangzhou Zhang Shi; Xianbei Qifu Guoren; Xianbei Tufa Wugu; self-appointed King of Liang Li Gao; Lushui Hu Juqu Mengxun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi, self-appointed Governor of Liangzhou; the Xianbei Qifu Guoren and Tufa Wugu; Li Gao, self-appointed King of Liang; and Juqu Mengxun of the Lushui Hu.

sentences.zh: 寔代統任，愍帝拜為使持節、都督涼州諸軍事、西中郎將、涼州刺史、領護羌校尉、西平公。

translations.literal: Shi succeeded to the command in his generation; Emperor Min appointed him bearer of the credentials of authority, commander-in-chief of all military affairs in Liangzhou, General of the Western Centre, Inspector of Liangzhou, concurrently Protector of the Di and Qiang, and Duke of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Shi inherited leadership of the domain, and Emperor Min invested him as bearer of the credentials of authority, commander-in-chief of all military affairs in Liangzhou, General of the Western Centre, Inspector of Liangzhou, Protector of the Di and Qiang, and Duke of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 劉曜陷長安，寔自稱侍中、司空、大都督、涼州牧，承制行事。

translations.literal: When Liu Yao captured Chang'an, Shi styled himself Attendant-in-Chief, Minister of Works, Grand Commander-in-Chief, and Governor of Liangzhou, and conducted affairs by imperial mandate.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Yao took Chang'an, Shi assumed the titles Attendant-in-Chief, Minister of Works, Grand Commander-in-Chief, and Governor of Liangzhou, and governed on the authority of the throne.

sentences.zh: 于時天下喪亂，秦雍之民死者十八九，唯涼州獨全。

translations.literal: At that time the realm was in turmoil; eight or nine tenths of the people of Qin and Yong perished, and Liangzhou alone remained intact.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was then in chaos, and eight or nine out of ten people in Qin and Yong died, while Liangzhou alone was spared.

sentences.zh: 寔自恃眾強，轉為驕恣。

translations.literal: Shi relied on his strength in numbers and gradually became arrogant and willful.
translations.idiomatic: Confident in his military strength, Shi grew increasingly arrogant and overbearing.

sentences.zh: 平文皇帝四年，寔為左右閻沙等所殺。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Emperor Pingwen, Shi was killed by his attendants Yan Sha and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Emperor Pingwen's reign, Shi was assassinated by his close attendants Yan Sha and his associates.

sentences.zh: 先是謠曰：「蛇利砲，蛇利砲，公頭墜地而不覺。」

translations.literal: Earlier a rhyme had said: 'She li pao, she li pao—the lord's head falls to the ground and he does not know it.'
translations.idiomatic: A rhyme had earlier run: 'Serpent's profit, serpent's profit—the lord's head drops to the ground and he never knows it.'

sentences.zh: 寔所住室梁間有人象而無頭，久之乃滅。

translations.literal: In the beams of the room where Shi lived there appeared a human figure without a head; after a long while it vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Between the beams of Shi's chamber there appeared a headless human figure, which after some time disappeared.

sentences.zh: 寔惡之，未幾見殺。

translations.literal: Shi hated this; before long he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Shi took this as an ill omen, and not long afterward he was slain.

sentences.zh: 寔弟茂統任。

translations.literal: Shi's younger brother Mao succeeded to the command.
translations.idiomatic: Shi's younger brother Mao took over leadership of the domain.

sentences.zh: 茂字成遜，私署使持節、都督涼州諸軍事、平西將軍、護羌校尉、涼州牧、西平公。

translations.literal: Mao, style name Chengxun, self-appointed himself bearer of the credentials of authority, commander-in-chief of all military affairs in Liangzhou, General Who Pacifies the West, Protector of the Di and Qiang, Governor of Liangzhou, and Duke of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Mao, whose style was Chengxun, styled himself bearer of the credentials of authority, commander-in-chief of all military affairs in Liangzhou, General Who Pacifies the West, Protector of the Di and Qiang, Governor of Liangzhou, and Duke of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 誅閻沙等百餘人。

translations.literal: He executed Yan Sha and more than a hundred others.
translations.idiomatic: He put Yan Sha and more than a hundred accomplices to death.

sentences.zh: 遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to pay court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched envoys to offer tribute at court.

sentences.zh: 茂妻弟賈模兄弟謀害茂，[1]茂殺之。

translations.literal: Mao's wife's younger brothers Jia Mo and his brothers plotted to kill Mao;[1] Mao killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Mo and his brothers, younger brothers of Mao's wife, conspired against Mao;[1] Mao had them executed.

sentences.zh: 劉曜上隴，茂懼而降，曜以為太師、涼王。

translations.literal: Liu Yao advanced into Long, Mao feared and submitted, and Yao appointed him Grand Preceptor and King of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yao marched into Long, Mao submitted in fear, and Yao made him Grand Preceptor and King of Liang.

sentences.zh: 茂卒，無子，寔子駿統任。

translations.literal: When Mao died without sons, Shi's son Jun succeeded to the command.
translations.idiomatic: Mao died childless, and Shi's son Jun inherited the domain.

sentences.zh: 駿，字公庭，自稱使持節、大將軍、護羌校尉、涼州牧、西平公。

translations.literal: Jun, style name Gongting, styled himself bearer of the credentials of authority, Grand General, Protector of the Di and Qiang, Governor of Liangzhou, and Duke of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Jun, whose style was Gongting, took the titles bearer of the credentials of authority, Grand General, Protector of the Di and Qiang, Governor of Liangzhou, and Duke of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to pay court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched envoys to offer tribute at court.

sentences.zh: 煬帝時，隴西人辛晏以枹罕降之，駿遂有河南之地，至於狄道，與石勒分境。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Yang, the Longxi man Xin Yan surrendered Fuhan to him; Jun then held the lands south of the Yellow River as far as Didao and divided the frontier with Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Yang's reign, Xin Yan of Longxi surrendered Fuhan to Jun, who thereby gained territory south of the Yellow River as far as Didao and shared a border with Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 駿築南城，起謙光殿於其中，窮珍極巧，又四面各起一殿，東曰宜陽青殿，南曰朱陽赤殿，西曰正德白殿，北曰玄武黑殿，服章器物皆依色隨四時居之，其旁有直省寺署，一依方色。

translations.literal: Jun built the Southern City and erected the Hall of Modest Brilliance within it, exhausting rare treasures and utmost craft; on all four sides he raised a hall each—the east called the Azure Hall of Yiyang, the south the Scarlet Hall of Zhuyang, the west the White Hall of Zhengde, the north the Black Hall of Xuanwu—and garments, regalia, and utensils all followed the colors as he dwelt according to the four seasons; beside them were direct offices and monasteries, all arranged by directional color.
translations.idiomatic: Jun constructed the Southern City and built within it the Hall of Modest Brilliance, lavishing the rarest materials and the finest workmanship. On each of the four sides he raised a separate hall: to the east the Azure Hall of Yiyang, to the south the Scarlet Hall of Zhuyang, to the west the White Hall of Zhengde, and to the north the Black Hall of Xuanwu. Robes, insignia, and furnishings all matched these colors, and he moved his residence with the seasons. Adjacent government offices and temples were likewise arranged according to the colors of the four directions.

sentences.zh: 其奢僭如此，民以勞怨。

translations.literal: His extravagance and presumption were such that the people were worn out and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: His extravagance and presumption went so far that the people were exhausted and full of resentment.

sentences.zh: 駿議治石田，參軍索孚諫曰：「凡為治者，動不逆天機，作不破地德。

translations.literal: Jun proposed to cultivate stony fields; the staff officer Suo Fu remonstrated, saying: 'In all governance, one must not act against Heaven's design, nor undertake works that violate the earth's virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Jun proposed turning rocky ground into farmland. His staff officer Suo Fu remonstrated: 'Whoever governs must not act against Heaven's design or undertake works that violate the earth's virtue.

sentences.zh: 昔后稷之播百穀，不墾磐石；

translations.literal: In antiquity Hou Ji sowed the hundred grains but did not plow bedrock;
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Hou Ji sowed the hundred grains but never plowed bedrock;

sentences.zh: 禹決江河，不逆流勢。

translations.literal: Yu cut through the rivers but did not go against their current.
translations.idiomatic: Yu cut through the rivers but never fought the current's flow.

sentences.zh: 今欲徙石為田，運土殖穀，計所損用，畝盈百石，所收不過三石而已，竊所未安。」

translations.literal: Now you wish to move stone to make fields, transport earth to plant grain—by my reckoning the cost per mu will exceed a hundred piculs, while the harvest will be no more than three piculs; this I cannot find reassuring.'
translations.idiomatic: Now you propose to shift stone to make fields and haul earth to plant grain. By my reckoning the cost per mu will exceed a hundred piculs while the harvest will be no more than three—I cannot see how this can be justified.'

sentences.zh: 駿怒，出孚為伊吾都尉。

translations.literal: Jun was angry and transferred Fu to be commandant of Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was furious and banished Fu to the post of commandant of Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 有石隕於破胡，燋而碎，聲如擊鼓，聞七百里。

translations.literal: A stone fell at Pohu, burned and shattered; the sound was like beating drums and was heard for seven hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: A meteorite fell at Pohu, burst into flame, and shattered; the sound was like thundering drums and carried seven hundred li.

sentences.zh: 其處氣上黑如煙，煙首如赤飊。

translations.literal: At that place vapour rose black as smoke, and the head of the smoke was like a crimson whirlwind.
translations.idiomatic: Black smoke rose from the site, its crest twisting like a crimson whirlwind.

sentences.zh: 駿少而淫佚，常夜出微行，姦亂邑里，少年皆化之。

translations.literal: Jun from youth was dissolute; he often went out at night in disguise, debauching the neighborhoods, and the young men all took him as their model.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Jun was dissolute, often slipping out at night in disguise to debauch the neighborhoods, and the young men of the city all followed his example.

sentences.zh: 性又貪惏。

translations.literal: His nature was also greedy and grasping.
translations.idiomatic: He was greedy and grasping by nature as well.

sentences.zh: 有圖秦隴意。

translations.literal: He had designs on Qin and Long.
translations.idiomatic: He harbored ambitions to conquer Qin and Long.

sentences.zh: 以穀帛付民，歲收倍利，利不充者，簿賣田宅。

translations.literal: He lent grain and cloth to the people and collected double interest yearly; those who could not pay had their fields and houses registered and sold.
translations.idiomatic: He lent grain and cloth to the people at double annual interest; those who could not repay had their land and homes seized and sold off the books.

sentences.zh: 分武威、武興、西平、張掖、酒泉、建康、西海、西郡、湟河、晉興、廣武十一郡為涼州，以長子重華為刺史；

translations.literal: He divided the eleven commanderies Wuwei, Wuxing, Xiping, Zhangye, Jiuquan, Jiankang, Xihai, Xijun, Huanghe, Jinxing, and Guangwu into Liangzhou and appointed his eldest son Chonghua inspector;
translations.idiomatic: He organized the eleven commanderies of Wuwei, Wuxing, Xiping, Zhangye, Jiuquan, Jiankang, Xihai, Xijun, Huanghe, Jinxing, and Guangwu as Liangzhou and appointed his eldest son Chonghua as inspector;

sentences.zh: 興晉、金城、[2]武始、南安、永晉、大夏、武城、漢中八郡為河州，以其寧戎校尉張瓘為刺史；

translations.literal: He established the eight commanderies Xingjin, Jincheng,[2] Wushi, Nan'an, Yongjin, Daxia, Wucheng, and Hanzhong as Hezhou and appointed his Pacifier of the Rong Zhang Guan inspector;
translations.idiomatic: He organized the eight commanderies of Xingjin, Jincheng,[2] Wushi, Nan'an, Yongjin, Daxia, Wucheng, and Hanzhong as Hezhou and appointed his Pacifier of the Rong, Zhang Guan, as inspector;

sentences.zh: 敦煌、晉昌、高昌，西域都護、戊己校尉、玉門大護軍，三郡三營為沙州，以西胡校尉楊宣為刺史。

translations.literal: Dunhuang, Jinchang, and Gaochang, together with the Protectorate of the Western Regions, the Wuji Commandant, and the Grand Protector of Yumen—the three commanderies and three garrisons—he made Shazhou and appointed the Commandant of the Western Barbarians Yang Xuan inspector.
translations.idiomatic: He grouped Dunhuang, Jinchang, and Gaochang together with the Protectorate of the Western Regions, the Wuji Commandant, and the Grand Protector of Yumen into Shazhou and appointed Yang Xuan, Commandant of the Western Barbarians, as inspector.

sentences.zh: 駿私署大都督、大將軍、假涼王、督攝三州。

translations.literal: Jun self-appointed himself Grand Commander-in-Chief, Grand General, Acting King of Liang, and supervisor of the three provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Jun styled himself Grand Commander-in-Chief, Grand General, Acting King of Liang, and overseer of all three provinces.

sentences.zh: 始置諸祭酒、郎中、大夫、舍人、謁者之官，官號皆擬天朝，而微辨其名。

translations.literal: He first established the offices of Libationers, Gentlemen, Grand Masters, Attendants, and Ushers; the titles all imitated the imperial court but were slightly differentiated in name.
translations.idiomatic: He first created the offices of Libationers, Gentlemen, Grandees, Attendants, and Ushers, modeling their titles on the imperial court but with slight variations in naming.

sentences.zh: 舞六佾，建豹尾，車服旌旗一如王者。

translations.literal: He performed the six-row dance, erected the leopard-tail banner, and made chariots, robes, and standards identical to those of a king.
translations.idiomatic: He performed the six-row royal dance, raised the leopard-tail banner, and equipped his chariots, robes, and standards in full royal fashion.

sentences.zh: 軌保涼州，陰澹之力，駿以陰氏門宗強盛，忌之，乃逼澹弟鑒令自殺，由是大失人情。

translations.literal: Gui had preserved Liangzhou through the power of Yin Dan; Jun, because the Yin clan's lineage was strong, envied them and forced Dan's younger brother Jian to kill himself, thereby greatly losing popular support.
translations.idiomatic: Gui had held Liangzhou thanks to Yin Dan's strength. Jun, jealous of the Yin's powerful clan, forced Dan's younger brother Jian to commit suicide and thereby lost the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 駿既病，見鑒為祟，遂死，時建國九年也。

translations.literal: When Jun fell ill he saw Jian as a haunting spirit and then died; it was the ninth year of the state.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun fell ill he was haunted by visions of Jian and soon died, in the ninth year of the state.

sentences.zh: 子重華統任。

translations.literal: His son Chonghua succeeded to the command.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chonghua inherited the domain.

sentences.zh: 重華，字太林。

translations.literal: Chonghua, style name Tailin.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghua, whose style was Tailin.

sentences.zh: 私署使持節、大都督、太尉公、護羌校尉、涼州牧、西平公、[3]假涼王。

translations.literal: He self-appointed himself bearer of the credentials of authority, Grand Commander-in-Chief, Grand Commandant, Protector of the Di and Qiang, Governor of Liangzhou, Duke of Xiping,[3] and Acting King of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He styled himself bearer of the credentials of authority, Grand Commander-in-Chief, Grand Commandant, Protector of the Di and Qiang, Governor of Liangzhou, Duke of Xiping,[3] and Acting King of Liang.

sentences.zh: 石虎遣麻秋率眾渡河，城於長最，涼州震動。

translations.literal: Shi Hu sent Ma Qiu to lead troops across the river and build a fortress at Changzui; Liangzhou was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu sent Ma Qiu with an army across the river to fortify Changzui, throwing Liangzhou into alarm.

sentences.zh: 司馬張耽薦主簿謝艾於重華，重華任之。

translations.literal: The Major Zhang Dan recommended the Registrar Xie Ai to Chonghua, and Chonghua employed him.
translations.idiomatic: Major Zhang Dan recommended the registrar Xie Ai to Chonghua, who put him in command.

sentences.zh: 艾擊斬秋將綦毌安等，俘斬萬五千人。

translations.literal: Ai attacked and killed Qiu's generals Qi Wuan and others, capturing and slaying fifteen thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Ai routed Ma Qiu's forces, killing his generals Qi Wuan and others and capturing or slaying fifteen thousand men.

sentences.zh: 重華遣使朝貢，自署丞相、涼王、領秦雍涼三州牧。

translations.literal: Chonghua sent envoys to pay court tribute and styled himself Chancellor, King of Liang, and Governor of the three provinces Qin, Yong, and Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghua sent envoys to court and styled himself Chancellor, King of Liang, and Governor of Qin, Yong, and Liang.

sentences.zh: 重華死，子曜靈統任。

translations.literal: When Chonghua died, his son Yaoling succeeded to the command.
translations.idiomatic: After Chonghua's death, his son Yaoling inherited the domain.

sentences.zh: 曜靈，年十歲。

translations.literal: Yaoling was ten years old.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoling was only ten years old.

sentences.zh: 自稱大司馬、涼州牧，以重華兄祚為撫軍將軍輔政。

translations.literal: He styled himself Grand Marshal and Governor of Liangzhou and made Chonghua's elder brother Zuo General Who Pacifies the Army to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: He took the titles Grand Marshal and Governor of Liangzhou and appointed Chonghua's elder brother Zuo, General Who Pacifies the Army, to assist in governing.

sentences.zh: 祚先蒸重華母馬氏，密說馬氏以曜靈幼弱，須立長君，馬從之，遂廢曜靈而立祚。

translations.literal: Zuo had earlier violated Chonghua's mother, Lady Ma; he secretly urged Lady Ma that Yaoling was young and weak and a mature ruler must be installed; Ma agreed, and they deposed Yaoling and enthroned Zuo.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo had earlier violated Chonghua's mother, Lady Ma. He secretly persuaded her that Yaoling was too young to rule and that an elder must be enthroned. Lady Ma agreed, Yaoling was deposed, and Zuo took the throne.

sentences.zh: 曜靈尋為祚所殺。

translations.literal: Before long Yaoling was killed by Zuo.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoling was soon murdered by Zuo.

sentences.zh: 祚，字太伯。

translations.literal: Zuo, style name Taibo.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo, whose style was Taibo.

sentences.zh: 既統任，自稱大將軍、涼州牧、涼公。

translations.literal: Once he held command he styled himself Grand General, Governor of Liangzhou, and Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Once in power he styled himself Grand General, Governor of Liangzhou, and Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 專為姦虐，駿及重華子女未嫁者皆淫之，涼州人士咸賦牆茨。

translations.literal: He devoted himself to debauchery and cruelty, violating all the unmarried sons and daughters of Jun and Chonghua; the gentlemen of Liangzhou all composed the 'Wall-Thatch' poem.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to cruelty and debauchery, violating every unmarried child of Jun and Chonghua. The gentry of Liangzhou composed the 'Wall-Thatch' ballad in protest.

sentences.zh: 初，重華末年，有螽斯蟲集安昌門外，緣壁逆行。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the last years of Chonghua, locusts gathered outside the Gate of Secure Prosperity and crawled up the wall in reverse.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Chonghua's reign, locusts gathered outside the Gate of Secure Prosperity and crawled up the wall in reverse.

sentences.zh: 都尉常據諫曰：「螽斯是祚小字，今乃逆行，災之大者，願出之。」

translations.literal: The Commandant Chang Ju remonstrated: 'The locust is Zuo's childhood name; now it moves in reverse—this is a great omen of disaster. I beg that he be sent away.'
translations.idiomatic: Commandant Chang Ju remonstrated: 'Locust is Zuo's childhood name, and now it moves backward—a grave omen. I beg that he be removed from court.'

sentences.zh: 重華曰：「子孫繁昌之徵，何為災也？

translations.literal: Chonghua said: 'It is a sign that descendants will flourish—how can it be a disaster?
translations.idiomatic: Chonghua replied: 'It is a sign that descendants will flourish—how can that be a disaster?

sentences.zh: 吾昨夢祚攝位，方委以周公之事，輔翼世子。」

translations.literal: Last night I dreamed that Zuo would hold the regency; I am just now entrusting him with the affairs of the Duke of Zhou to assist the heir.'
translations.idiomatic: I dreamed last night that Zuo would hold the regency. I am entrusting him with the Duke of Zhou's role—to assist the heir.'

sentences.zh: 而祚終殺曜靈焉。

translations.literal: Yet in the end Zuo killed Yaoling.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the end Zuo murdered Yaoling.

sentences.zh: 自署涼王，立宗廟，置百官，號和平元年。

translations.literal: He styled himself King of Liang, established ancestral temples, installed the full bureaucracy, and proclaimed the first year of Peace.
translations.idiomatic: He styled himself King of Liang, established ancestral temples, installed a full bureaucracy, and proclaimed the first year of the Peace era.

sentences.zh: 遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to pay court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched envoys to offer tribute at court.

sentences.zh: 又追加軌以下王號。

translations.literal: He also posthumously added royal titles for Gui and those below him.
translations.idiomatic: He also posthumously conferred royal titles on Gui and his successors.

sentences.zh: 濫殺謝艾於酒泉。

translations.literal: He wantonly killed Xie Ai at Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: He had Xie Ai executed without cause at Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 郎中丁琪諫祚僭竊，祚斬琪於闕下。

translations.literal: The Gentleman Ding Qi remonstrated against Zuo's usurpation; Zuo executed Qi below the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman Ding Qi remonstrated against Zuo's usurpation; Zuo had him beheaded below the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 廢諸神祀，山川枯竭。

translations.literal: He abolished all divine sacrifices; rivers and mountains ran dry.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished sacrifices to the gods, and rivers and springs dried up.

sentences.zh: 置五都尉，司人姦過。

translations.literal: He established five commandants to oversee people's crimes and transgressions.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed five commandants to spy on the people's crimes and transgressions.

sentences.zh: 禁四品以下不得衣繒帛，庶人不得畜奴婢、乘車馬。

translations.literal: He forbade those below the fourth rank to wear silk; commoners were not allowed to keep slaves or maidservants or ride in chariots or on horses.
translations.idiomatic: He forbade officials below the fourth rank to wear silk, and commoners were barred from keeping slaves, riding horses, or driving chariots.

sentences.zh: 百姓怨憤。

translations.literal: The common people were resentful and angry.
translations.idiomatic: The people seethed with resentment.

sentences.zh: 有光狀如車蓋，聲如雷，震動城邑。

translations.literal: There was a light shaped like a carriage canopy; the sound was like thunder and shook the cities.
translations.idiomatic: A light shaped like a carriage canopy appeared, thunder shook the cities, and the earth trembled.

sentences.zh: 仲夏降霜。

translations.literal: In midsummer frost fell.
translations.idiomatic: Frost fell in midsummer.

sentences.zh: 有神降自稱「玄冥」，與人交語，祚日夜祈之，神言與其福利，祚信焉。

translations.literal: A spirit descended calling itself 'Dark Mystery,' conversing with people; Zuo prayed to it day and night; the spirit said it would grant him blessings, and Zuo believed it.
translations.idiomatic: A spirit descended claiming to be 'Dark Mystery' and spoke with men. Zuo prayed to it day and night; the spirit promised him blessings, and Zuo believed every word.

sentences.zh: 眾知祚必敗，而祚暴虐彌甚。

translations.literal: All knew Zuo must fall, yet his cruelty grew ever worse.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone knew Zuo was doomed, yet his cruelty only grew worse.

sentences.zh: 明年，祚河州刺史張瓘起兵討祚，驍騎將軍宋混率眾應瓘。

translations.literal: The next year Zhang Guan, Inspector of Hezhou under Zuo, raised troops to attack Zuo; the Valiant Cavalry General Song Hun led forces to join Guan.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Zhang Guan, Zuo's inspector of Hezhou, raised an army against him, and Valiant Cavalry General Song Hun marched to his support.

sentences.zh: 混進攻姑臧，祚遣侍中索孚伐瓘。

translations.literal: Hun advanced to attack Guzang; Zuo sent the Attendant-in-Chief Suo Fu to attack Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Song Hun advanced on Guzang while Zuo sent Attendant-in-Chief Suo Fu to attack Zhang Guan.

sentences.zh: 有王鸞者，云「師出必敗」，并陳祚三不道。

translations.literal: There was a Wang Luan who said, 'If the army goes forth it will surely be defeated,' and also set forth Zuo's three iniquities.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Wang Luan declared, 'The army will surely be defeated if it marches out,' and enumerated Zuo's three great crimes.

sentences.zh: 祚以妖言惑眾，斬之，鸞臨刑曰：「我死之後，軍敗於外，王死於內。」

translations.literal: Zuo charged him with using demonic words to delude the masses and executed him; at execution Luan said: 'After I die, the army will be defeated outside and the king will die within.'
translations.idiomatic: Zuo charged him with spreading sedition and had him executed. At the block Wang Luan cried: 'After I die, the army will be defeated without and the king will die within.'

sentences.zh: 祚族之。

translations.literal: Zuo exterminated his clan.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo exterminated his entire clan.

sentences.zh: 宋混至姑臧，領軍趙長等開宮門應之。

translations.literal: When Song Hun reached Guzang, the camp commander Zhao Chang and others opened the palace gates to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When Song Hun reached Guzang, Camp Commander Zhao Chang and others opened the palace gates to admit him.

sentences.zh: 入殿稱萬歲，祚以長等破混也，出勞之。

translations.literal: They entered the hall and shouted 'Long live the king!'; Zuo thought Chang and the others had defeated Hun and came out to reward them.
translations.idiomatic: They entered the hall shouting 'Long live the king!' Zuo, thinking Zhao Chang had defeated Song Hun, came out to congratulate them.

sentences.zh: 長以槊刺祚中額，祚奔入，為厨士徐黑所殺，暴尸道左。

translations.literal: Chang stabbed Zuo in the forehead with a spear; Zuo fled inside and was killed by the kitchen servant Xu Hei; his corpse was left exposed on the left of the road.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chang drove a spear into Zuo's forehead. Zuo fled inside but was killed by the kitchen servant Xu Hei, and his body was left in the street.

sentences.zh: 城內咸稱萬歲。

translations.literal: Throughout the city all shouted 'Long live the king!'
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the city people shouted 'Long live the king!'

sentences.zh: 瓘等立重華少子玄靖統任。

translations.literal: Guan and the others enthroned Chonghua's youngest son Xuanjing to succeed to the command.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guan and his allies enthroned Chonghua's youngest son Xuanjing as ruler.

sentences.zh: 玄靖，字元安。

translations.literal: Xuanjing, style name Yuan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanjing, whose style was Yuan'an.

sentences.zh: 自署使持節、大都督、大將軍、涼王。

translations.literal: He styled himself bearer of the credentials of authority, Grand Commander-in-Chief, Grand General, and King of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He styled himself bearer of the credentials of authority, Grand Commander-in-Chief, Grand General, and King of Liang.

sentences.zh: 以瓘為尚書令、涼州牧秉政，宋混為尚書僕射。

translations.literal: He made Guan Director of the Masters of Writing and Governor of Liangzhou to hold government, and Song Hun Vice-Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Zhang Guan Director of the Masters of Writing and Governor of Liangzhou to govern, with Song Hun as Vice-Director.

sentences.zh: 瓘性猜惡，賞罰皆以愛憎，無復綱紀。

translations.literal: Guan's nature was suspicious and vicious; rewards and punishments all followed personal likes and dislikes, and there was no longer any order.
translations.idiomatic: Guan was suspicious and cruel by nature, meting out rewards and punishments according to personal favor, and government fell into chaos.

sentences.zh: 郎中殷郇陳損益，諫瓘，瓘曰：「虎生三日能食肉，不須人教。」

translations.literal: The Gentleman Yin Huan set forth what should be added or reduced and remonstrated with Guan; Guan said: 'A tiger three days after birth can eat meat—it needs no one to teach it.'
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman Yin Huan offered advice on policy and remonstrated with Guan, who replied: 'A tiger can eat meat three days after it is born—it needs no teacher.'

sentences.zh: 由是莫有言者。

translations.literal: From this no one spoke further.
translations.idiomatic: After that no one dared speak up.

sentences.zh: 瓘與玄靖參乘出城，城北大橋三梁俱折。

translations.literal: When Guan and Xuanjing rode out of the city together, all three beams of the great northern bridge broke.
translations.idiomatic: When Guan and Xuanjing rode out of the city together, all three beams of the great bridge north of the city snapped.

sentences.zh: 瓘惡之，乃日日散錢帛，樹私惠，而都街殺人，朝朝不絕。

translations.literal: Guan hated this; he then daily scattered money and cloth to cultivate private favor, while in the capital streets killings went on without cease morning after morning.
translations.idiomatic: Guan took this as an ill omen and began scattering money and cloth daily to buy favor, even as executions in the capital streets continued without pause.

sentences.zh: 思為亂者十室而九。

translations.literal: Of every ten households, nine thought of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Nine households in ten were plotting revolt.

sentences.zh: 東苑大冢上忽有池水；

translations.literal: On the great mound in the Eastern Park water suddenly appeared as a pool;
translations.idiomatic: A pool of water suddenly appeared atop the great mound in the Eastern Park;

sentences.zh: 城東大澤，地忽火燃，廣數里。

translations.literal: in the great marsh east of the city the ground suddenly burst into flame over several li.
translations.idiomatic: and east of the city in the great marsh the ground burst into flame over several li.

sentences.zh: 乃殺宿嫌牛旋等以應水火之變。

translations.literal: He then killed his old enemies Niu Xuan and others to respond to the transformations of water and fire.
translations.idiomatic: Guan killed his old enemies Niu Xuan and others to appease these omens of water and fire.

sentences.zh: 瓘謀誅諸宋，廢玄靖自立。

translations.literal: Guan plotted to execute the Song clan, depose Xuanjing, and enthrone himself.
translations.idiomatic: Guan plotted to destroy the Song clan, depose Xuanjing, and seize the throne himself.

sentences.zh: 先是，太白守輿鬼，占者以為州分，當有暴兵，故瓘欲厭之。

translations.literal: Earlier Venus had lodged in the Ghost asterism; diviners held that a commandery division would suffer violent troops, so Guan wished to avert it.
translations.idiomatic: Venus had earlier lodged in the Ghost asterism, and diviners predicted violent upheaval in the region—Guan sought to avert the omen by bloodshed.

sentences.zh: 於是宋混率眾誅瓘，瓘先殺妻子三十口，乃自殺。

translations.literal: Thereupon Song Hun led forces to execute Guan; Guan first killed his wife and children, thirty persons in all, then killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Song Hun then led his forces against Guan, who first slaughtered his wife and children—thirty souls in all—then took his own life.

sentences.zh: 玄靖以混為驃騎大將軍、尚書令。

translations.literal: Xuanjing made Hun General of Agile Cavalry and Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanjing appointed Song Hun General of Agile Cavalry and Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 混病死，弟玄安代輔政。

translations.literal: When Hun died of illness, his younger brother Xuan'an replaced him in assisting government.
translations.idiomatic: When Song Hun died of illness, his younger brother Xuan'an took over as chief minister.

sentences.zh: 以旱祈帶石山，玄安欲登之，弟名犯世宗諱曰：「世人云登此山者破家身亡。」

translations.literal: Because of drought they prayed at Mount Daishi; Xuan'an wished to ascend it. A younger brother whose name violated the taboo name of Emperor Shizong said: "People say that whoever climbs this mountain will have his household destroyed and lose his life."
translations.idiomatic: During a drought they prayed at Mount Daishi, and Xuan'an wanted to climb it. A younger brother whose given name violated the taboo of Emperor Shizong warned: "People say that whoever ascends this peak will bring ruin on his house and lose his life."

sentences.zh: 玄安曰：「安有此也！」

translations.literal: Xuan'an said: "How could there be such a thing!"
translations.idiomatic: Xuan'an replied: "Nonsense! How could such a thing be true?"

sentences.zh: 策馬登之，馬倒傷足。

translations.literal: He whipped his horse and climbed it; the horse fell and injured its leg.
translations.idiomatic: He spurred his horse up the mountain; the horse stumbled and broke its leg.

sentences.zh: 御史房屋柱自燃燋折，或曰：「柱之為字也，左木右主，『宋』字含木，木燋，宋破而主存，災之大也，宜防之。」

translations.literal: A pillar in the house of the clerk Fangwu spontaneously ignited, burned, and broke. Someone said: "As for the character zhu (pillar), it has wood on the left and lord on the right; the character 'Song' contains wood—when the wood burns, the Song clan is destroyed but the lord remains. This is a great calamity; one should guard against it."
translations.idiomatic: A pillar in the house of the clerk Fangwu burst into flame, charred, and snapped. Some said: "The character for 'pillar' has wood on the left and 'lord' on the right; the Song surname also contains the wood radical—when the wood burns away, the Song clan falls but the lord survives. This is a dire omen and should be heeded."

sentences.zh: 又所乘馬五匹，一夜中髭尾禿，人曰：「尾之為字也，尸下毛，毛去尸，絕滅之徵。」

translations.literal: Moreover, of the five horses he rode, overnight their manes and tails went bald. People said: "As for the character wei (tail), it has hair below a corpse; when the hair is removed from the corpse, it is a sign of extinction."
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, overnight the manes and tails of all five horses he rode went bald. People said: "The character for 'tail' puts hair beneath a corpse—strip the hair from the corpse and you have the sign of total annihilation."

sentences.zh: 玄安曰：「吉凶在天，知可如何。」

translations.literal: Xuan'an said: "Good and ill fortune lie with Heaven—what can one know?"
translations.idiomatic: Xuan'an said: "Fortune and disaster rest with Heaven—what can we know in advance?"

sentences.zh: 未幾，玄安司馬張邕起兵殺玄安，盡誅宋氏。

translations.literal: Before long, Xuan'an's Chief Commandant Zhang Yong raised troops, killed Xuan'an, and executed the entire Song clan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Xuan'an's Chief Commandant Zhang Yong rebelled, killed Xuan'an, and wiped out the entire Song clan.

sentences.zh: 先是謠曰：「滅宋者田土子。」

translations.literal: Earlier a rhyme had said: "He who destroys the Song is Tian Tuzi."
translations.idiomatic: A prophecy had earlier run: "The destroyer of Song is Tian Tuzi."

sentences.zh: 邕，一名野。

translations.literal: Yong was also named Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Yong also went by the name Ye.

sentences.zh: 邕刑殺過差，內外復思為亂，駿少子天錫因民心起兵殺邕，以冠軍大將軍輔政。

translations.literal: Yong's punishments and killings were excessive; within and without, people again thought of rebellion. Jun's youngest son Tianxi, relying on popular sentiment, raised troops and killed Yong, then served as regent as General of the Champion.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's executions grew increasingly brutal, and discontent spread inside and outside the court. Jun's youngest son Tianxi rallied popular support, rose in arms, and killed Yong, then governed as regent with the title General of the Champion.

sentences.zh: 玄靖庶母郭氏以天錫擅權，與張氏疏宗謀誅之，事發，天錫殺玄靖而自立。

translations.literal: Xuanjing's concubine mother, Lady Guo, because Tianxi monopolized power, plotted with distant members of the Zhang clan to kill him. When the affair was exposed, Tianxi killed Xuanjing and enthroned himself.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanjing's concubine mother, Lady Guo, resenting Tianxi's seizure of power, conspired with distant Zhang clansmen to kill him. When the plot was discovered, Tianxi killed Xuanjing and took the throne himself.

sentences.zh: 天錫，字純嘏，一名公純。

translations.literal: Tianxi, style name Chungu, was also called Gongchun.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxi, whose style was Chungu, was also known as Gongchun.

sentences.zh: 私署使持節、大都督、大將軍、護羌校尉、涼州牧、涼王。

translations.literal: He self-appointed himself bearer of the credentials of authority, Grand Commander-in-Chief, Grand General, Protector of the Di and Qiang, Governor of Liangzhou, and King of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He styled himself bearer of the credentials of authority, Grand Commander-in-Chief, Grand General, Protector of the Di and Qiang, Governor of Liangzhou, and King of Liang.

sentences.zh: 有火燃於泥中。

translations.literal: Fire burned within mud.
translations.idiomatic: Fire was seen burning within mud.

sentences.zh: 天錫驕恣淫昏，不恤民務，元日與嬖人褻飲。

translations.literal: Tianxi was arrogant, willful, dissolute, and muddled; he did not care for the people's affairs. On New Year's Day he drank lewdly with his favorites.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxi grew arrogant, dissolute, and heedless of state affairs. On New Year's Day he caroused indecently with his favorites.

sentences.zh: 既。

translations.literal: When it was over.
translations.idiomatic: When the revelry was over.

sentences.zh: □□羣臣朝賀，又不省其母。

translations.literal: The ministers came to offer New Year congratulations, yet he still did not visit his mother.
translations.idiomatic: When the ministers came to offer New Year congratulations, he still neglected to pay respects to his mother.

sentences.zh: 從事中郎張慮輿櫬切諫，且求大覲，天錫不納。

translations.literal: Attendant Gentleman Zhang Lu, carrying his own coffin, remonstrated sharply and also requested a formal audience; Tianxi would not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Gentleman Zhang Lu came bearing his own coffin to remonstrate forcefully and beg for a formal audience; Tianxi refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 昭成末，苻堅遣將苟萇伐涼州，破之，天錫降於萇。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhaocheng reign, Fu Jian sent the general Gou Chang to attack Liangzhou, defeated it, and Tianxi surrendered to Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Emperor Zhaocheng's reign, Fu Jian dispatched General Gou Chang against Liangzhou, broke the state, and Tianxi surrendered to him.

sentences.zh: 初駿時謠曰：「劉新婦簸米，石新婦炊羖，羝蕩滌，簸張兒，張兒食之口正披。」

translations.literal: During Jun's time a rhyme said: "Liu's new bride winnows rice; Shi's new bride cooks mutton; the ram washes the trough, winnows Zhang's child—Zhang's child eats and his mouth splits open."
translations.idiomatic: In Jun's day a rhyme ran: "Liu's new bride winnows rice; Shi's new bride cooks mutton; the ram washes the trough and winnows Zhang's child—Zhang's child eats, and his mouth splits wide."

sentences.zh: 是時姑臧及諸郡國童兒皆歌之，謂劉曜、石虎並伐涼州不克，至堅而降之也。

translations.literal: At that time children in Guzang and the various commanderies and kingdoms all sang it, meaning that Liu Yao and Shi Hu both attacked Liangzhou without success, but when Fu Jian came, it submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Children throughout Guzang and the surrounding commanderies sang it, foretelling that Liu Yao and Shi Hu would both fail to conquer Liangzhou, but that it would fall when Fu Jian came.

sentences.zh: 天錫至長安，堅拜為尚書。

translations.literal: When Tianxi reached Chang'an, Fu Jian appointed him Master of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: After Tianxi arrived in Chang'an, Fu Jian appointed him to the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 堅敗於壽春，天錫奔建康。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian was defeated at Shouchun, Tianxi fled to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu Jian's defeat at Shouchun, Tianxi fled to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑乞伏國仁，出於隴西。

translations.literal: The Xianbei Qifu Guoren came from Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Guoren of the Xianbei came from Longxi.

sentences.zh: 其先如弗自漠北南出。

translations.literal: His ancestor Rufu came south from the northern deserts.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Rufu had migrated south from the northern steppe.

sentences.zh: 五代祖祐隣并兼諸部，部眾漸盛。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Youlin annexed and absorbed the various tribes, and the tribal following gradually grew strong.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation ancestor Youlin absorbed neighboring tribes, and their following steadily grew.

sentences.zh: 父司繁，擁部落降於苻堅，以為南單于，又拜鎮西將軍，鎮勇士川。

translations.literal: His father Sifan, leading the tribes, submitted to Fu Jian and was made Southern Chanyu; he was also appointed General Who Guards the West and stationed at Yongshi River.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sifan led the tribes in submission to Fu Jian, who made him Southern Chanyu and also appointed him General Who Guards the West, with his seat at Yongshi River.

sentences.zh: 司繁死，國仁代統任。

translations.literal: When Sifan died, Guoren succeeded to the command.
translations.idiomatic: When Sifan died, Guoren took over leadership of the tribes.

sentences.zh: 苻堅之伐司馬昌明，以國仁為前將軍，領騎先鋒。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian attacked Sima Changming, he made Guoren Forward General and put him in command of the cavalry vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Jian marched against Sima Changming, he appointed Guoren Forward General and placed him at the head of the cavalry vanguard.

sentences.zh: 及堅之敗，國仁叔步頹叛於隴右，堅令國仁討之，步頹大悅，迎而推之，招集部落，眾十餘萬。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian was defeated, Guoren's uncle Butui rebelled in Longyou. Fu Jian ordered Guoren to suppress him, but Butui was greatly pleased, welcomed him, and pushed him forward; he gathered the tribes, and their numbers reached more than one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu Jian's defeat, Guoren's uncle Butui rebelled in Longyou. Fu Jian ordered Guoren to put him down, but Butui welcomed him instead and rallied the tribes behind him, gathering a following of more than one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 太祖時，私署大都督，大將軍，大單于，秦州、河州牧，號年建義，署置官屬，分部內為十一郡，築勇士城以都之。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Taizu, he self-appointed himself Grand Commander-in-Chief, Grand General, and Grand Chanyu, and Governor of Qin and He provinces; he adopted the era name Jianyi, appointed officials, divided the interior into eleven commanderies, and built Yongshi City as his capital.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Taizu's reign he styled himself Grand Commander-in-Chief, Grand General, and Grand Chanyu, and Governor of Qin and He provinces; he adopted the era name Jianyi, established a full bureaucracy, divided his territory into eleven commanderies, and built Yongshi City as his capital.

sentences.zh: 國仁死，弟乾歸統事，自署大都督、大將軍、大單于、河南王，改年為太初，署百官。

translations.literal: When Guoren died, his younger brother Qiangui took charge of affairs. He styled himself Grand Commander-in-Chief, Grand General, Grand Chanyu, and King of Henan; he changed the era name to Taichu and appointed the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: After Guoren's death, his younger brother Qiangui assumed leadership. He styled himself Grand Commander-in-Chief, Grand General, Grand Chanyu, and King of Henan, adopted the era name Taichu, and established a full court.

sentences.zh: 登國中，遷於金城。

translations.literal: In the middle of the Dengguo reign, he moved to Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Midway through the Dengguo reign he relocated his capital to Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 南門自壞，乾歸惡之，遷於苑川。

translations.literal: The southern gate collapsed of itself; Qiangui took this as ill and moved to Yuanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the southern gate collapsed on its own, Qiangui took it as a bad omen and moved his seat to Yuanchuan.

sentences.zh: 尋為姚興所破，又奔枹罕，遂降姚興，興拜為河州刺史，封歸義侯。

translations.literal: Soon he was defeated by Yao Xing, fled again to Fuhan, and then submitted to Yao Xing. Xing appointed him Inspector of He Province and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Guiyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon defeated by Yao Xing, fled to Fuhan, and submitted. Yao Xing appointed him Inspector of He Province and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Guiyi.

sentences.zh: 尋還苑川。

translations.literal: Soon he returned to Yuanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he returned to Yuanchuan.

sentences.zh: 乾歸乃背姚興，私稱秦王，置百官，年號更始。

translations.literal: Qiangui then turned against Yao Xing, privately styled himself King of Qin, appointed the hundred officials, and adopted the era name Gengshi.
translations.idiomatic: Qiangui then broke with Yao Xing, declared himself King of Qin, established a full court, and adopted the era name Gengshi.

sentences.zh: 遣使請援，太宗許之。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to request aid, and Emperor Taizong granted it.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to request aid, and Emperor Taizong agreed to help.

sentences.zh: 後乾歸田於五谿，梟集其手，尋為兄子公府所殺。

translations.literal: Later, while Qiangui was hunting at Wuxi, owls gathered on his hands; before long he was killed by his elder brother's son Gongfu.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while Qiangui was hunting at Wuxi, owls alighted on his hands—an ill omen. Before long his nephew Gongfu killed him.

sentences.zh: 子熾磐殺公府，代統位。

translations.literal: His son Chipan killed Gongfu and succeeded to the command.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chipan killed Gongfu and took the throne.

sentences.zh: 熾磐，自稱大將軍、河南王，改年為永康。

translations.literal: Chipan styled himself Grand General and King of Henan, and changed the era name to Yongkang.
translations.idiomatic: Chipan styled himself Grand General and King of Henan and adopted the era name Yongkang.

sentences.zh: 後襲禿髮傉檀於樂都，滅之，乃私署秦王，置百官，改年為建洪。

translations.literal: Later he attacked Tufa Rutan at Ledu and destroyed him; he then privately styled himself King of Qin, appointed the hundred officials, and changed the era name to Jianhong.
translations.idiomatic: He later attacked Tufa Rutan at Ledu and destroyed his state, then styled himself King of Qin, established a full court, and adopted the era name Jianhong.

sentences.zh: [4]後遣其尚書郎莫胡、[5]積射將軍乞伏又寅等貢黃金二百斤，請伐赫連昌，世祖許之。

translations.literal: [4] Later he sent his Master of Writing Attendant Mo Hu, [5] General of Accumulated Archers Qifu Youyin, and others to present two hundred jin of gold and request a campaign against Helian Chang; Emperor Shizu granted it.
translations.idiomatic: [4] He later sent his Master of Writing Attendant Mo Hu, [5] General of Accumulated Archers Qifu Youyin, and others with two hundred jin of gold, asking permission to attack Helian Chang; Emperor Shizu agreed.

sentences.zh: 及世祖平統萬，熾磐乃遣其叔平遠將軍泥頭、弟安遠將軍度質於京師，又使其中書侍郎王愷、丞相從事中郎烏訥闐奉表貢其方物。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu pacified Tongwan, Chipan then sent his uncle, General Who Pacifies the Distance Nitu, and his younger brother, General Who Pacifies from Afar Duzhi, to the capital; he also had his Secretariat Attendant Wang Kai and Attendant Gentleman of the Chancellor Wune Tian present a memorial and tribute of local products.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Shizu pacified Tongwan, Chipan sent his uncle Nitu, General Who Pacifies the Distance, and his younger brother Duzhi, General Who Pacifies from Afar, to the capital, along with Secretariat Attendant Wang Kai and Attendant Gentleman of the Chancellor Wune Tian bearing tribute and a memorial.

sentences.zh: 熾磐死，子暮末統任。

translations.literal: When Chipan died, his son Mumo succeeded to the command.
translations.idiomatic: After Chipan's death, his son Mumo took the throne.

sentences.zh: 暮末，字安石跋。

translations.literal: Mumo, style name Anshiba.
translations.idiomatic: Mumo, whose style was Anshiba.

sentences.zh: 既立，改年為永洪。

translations.literal: Once enthroned, he changed the era name to Yonghong.
translations.idiomatic: Upon taking the throne, he adopted the era name Yonghong.

sentences.zh: 其尚書隴西辛進曾隨熾磐遊於後園，進彈鳥丸，誤傷暮末母面，至是殺進五族二十七人。

translations.literal: His Master of Writing, Xin Jin of Longxi, had once accompanied Chipan on an outing in the rear garden; Jin shot a pellet and accidentally wounded Mumo's mother in the face. At this time Mumo killed Jin and twenty-seven members of five clans.
translations.idiomatic: His Master of Writing, Xin Jin of Longxi, had once joined Chipan on a stroll in the rear garden and, shooting a pellet, accidentally struck Mumo's mother in the face. Mumo now executed Jin and twenty-seven members of five clans.

sentences.zh: 暮末弟殊羅蒸熾磐左夫人禿髮氏，暮末知而禁之。

translations.literal: Mumo's younger brother Shuluo steamed Chipan's left consort, Lady Tufa; when Mumo learned of it, he forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: Mumo's younger brother Shuluo attempted to steam Chipan's left consort, Lady Tufa; when Mumo found out, he forbade it.

sentences.zh: 殊羅懼，與叔父什夤謀殺暮末。

translations.literal: Shuluo was afraid and, with his uncle Shiyin, plotted to kill Mumo.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing punishment, Shuluo conspired with his uncle Shiyin to assassinate Mumo.

sentences.zh: 禿髮氏盜門鑰於內，鑰誤，門者告暮末，收其黨與盡殺之。

translations.literal: Lady Tufa stole the gate key from within, but the key was wrong; the gatekeeper reported this to Mumo, who seized the conspirators and executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Tufa stole a gate key from inside the palace, but it was the wrong one; the gatekeeper alerted Mumo, who arrested the conspirators and had them all killed.

sentences.zh: 欲鞭什夤，什夤曰：「我負汝死，不負汝鞭。」

translations.literal: Mumo wished to flog Shiyin. Shiyin said: "I would rather die for you than submit to your lash."
translations.idiomatic: Mumo wanted to flog Shiyin, who said: "I would rather die for you than endure your whip."

sentences.zh: 暮末怒，刳其腹，投屍於河。

translations.literal: Mumo was enraged, disemboweled him, and cast his corpse into the river.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Mumo disemboweled him and threw his body into the river.

sentences.zh: 什夤母弟白養及去列頗有怨言，又殺之。

translations.literal: Shiyin's younger maternal brother Baiyang and Qulie voiced considerable resentment, and Mumo killed them as well.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyin's younger maternal brother Baiyang and Qulie murmured against him, and Mumo killed them too.

sentences.zh: 政刑酷濫，內外崩離，部民多叛，人思亂矣。

translations.literal: Government and punishments were cruel and excessive; within and without the state collapsed and split apart; many tribesmen rebelled, and people longed for chaos.
translations.idiomatic: His government grew cruel and arbitrary; the realm fractured within and without; tribesmen rebelled in numbers, and the people hungered for upheaval.

sentences.zh: 後為赫連定所逼，遣王愷、烏訥闐請迎於世祖，世祖許以安定以西、平涼以東封之。

translations.literal: Later, pressed by Helian Ding, he sent Wang Kai and Wune Tian to request that Emperor Shizu receive him; Emperor Shizu promised to enfeoff him with the territory west of Anding and east of Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: Later, hard pressed by Helian Ding, he sent Wang Kai and Wune Tian to ask Emperor Shizu to receive him; the emperor promised to enfeoff him with the lands west of Anding and east of Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 暮末乃焚城邑，毀寶器，率戶萬五千至高田谷，為赫連定所拒，遂保南安。

translations.literal: Mumo then burned the cities and towns, destroyed the precious vessels, and led fifteen thousand households to Gaotian Valley; blocked by Helian Ding, he then held Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Mumo burned his cities, destroyed his treasures, and led fifteen thousand households to Gaotian Valley; when Helian Ding blocked his path, he withdrew to defend Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 世祖遣使迎之，暮末衞將軍吉毗固諫，以為不宜內徙，暮末從之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu sent envoys to welcome him. Mumo's Guard General Ji Pi remonstrated firmly, holding that an inward relocation was inadvisable, and Mumo followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu sent envoys to welcome him, but Mumo's Guard General Ji Pi strongly advised against moving inland, and Mumo heeded him.

sentences.zh: 赫連定遣其北平公韋伐率眾一萬攻南安，城內大饑，人相食。

translations.literal: Helian Ding sent his Duke of Beiping, Wei Fa, to lead ten thousand men to attack Nan'an. Within the city there was severe famine, and people ate one another.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Ding dispatched his Duke of Beiping, Wei Fa, with ten thousand troops against Nan'an. Famine gripped the city, and people resorted to cannibalism.

sentences.zh: 神䴥四年，暮末及宗族五百餘人出降，送於上邽。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shenju, Mumo and more than five hundred members of his clan came out and surrendered; they were sent to Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Shenju, Mumo and more than five hundred of his clansmen surrendered and were sent to Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑禿髮烏孤，八世祖匹孤自塞北遷于河西。

translations.literal: The Xianbei Tufa Wugu—his eighth-generation ancestor Pigu had migrated from the northern frontier to Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: Tufa Wugu of the Xianbei traced his line to Pigu, who eight generations earlier had migrated from the northern frontier to Hexi.

sentences.zh: 其地東至麥田、牽屯，西至濕羅，南至澆河，北接大漠。

translations.literal: Their territory extended east to Maitian and Qiantun, west to Shiruo, south to the Jiao River, and north to the great desert.
translations.idiomatic: Their lands stretched east to Maitian and Qiantun, west to Shiruo, south to the Jiao River, and north to the great desert.

sentences.zh: 匹孤死，子壽闐統任。

translations.literal: When Pigu died, his son Shoutian succeeded to the command.
translations.idiomatic: After Pigu's death, his son Shoutian took over leadership of the tribe.

sentences.zh: 初母孕壽闐，因寢產於被中，乃名禿髮，其俗為被覆之義。

translations.literal: At first, when his mother was pregnant with Shoutian, she gave birth while asleep, wrapped in the bedding; therefore they were named Tufa, meaning in their custom 'covered by a quilt.'
translations.idiomatic: When his mother was pregnant with Shoutian, she gave birth in her sleep, still wrapped in the bedding—hence the name Tufa, which in their custom meant 'covered by a quilt.'

sentences.zh: 五世祖樹機能壯果多謀略，晉泰始中，殺秦州刺史胡烈於萬斛堆，[6]敗涼州刺史蘇愉于金山。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Shujineng was strong, resolute, and full of stratagems. In the Taishi era of Jin he killed the Inspector of Qin Province, Hu Lie, at Wandudui, [6] and defeated the Inspector of Liang Province, Su Yu, at Jinshan.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation ancestor Shujineng was a formidable and cunning warrior. During the Jin Taishi era he killed Hu Lie, Inspector of Qin Province, at Wandudui, [6] and routed Su Yu, Inspector of Liang Province, at Jinshan.

sentences.zh: 咸寧中，又斬涼州刺史楊欣於丹嶺，盡有涼州之地。

translations.literal: In the Xianning era he again beheaded the Inspector of Liang Province, Yang Xin, at Danling, and came to possess all the territory of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianning era he beheaded Yang Xin, Inspector of Liang Province, at Danling and seized all of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 後為部民沒骨所殺，從弟務丸統任。

translations.literal: Later he was killed by the tribesman Moguh; his younger cousin of the second degree Wuyuan succeeded to the command.
translations.idiomatic: He was later killed by the tribesman Moguh, and his second cousin Wuyuan took over leadership.

sentences.zh: 務丸曾孫思復犍，部眾稍盛，即烏孤父也。

translations.literal: Wuyuan's great-grandson Sifujian gradually grew strong in tribal following; he was Wugu's father.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyuan's great-grandson Sifujian steadily expanded the tribal following; he was Wugu's father.

sentences.zh: 思復犍死，烏孤統任。

translations.literal: When Sifujian died, Wugu succeeded to the command.
translations.idiomatic: After Sifujian's death, Wugu took over leadership of the tribe.

sentences.zh: 皇始初，呂光拜烏孤益州牧、左賢王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangshi, Lu Guang appointed Wugu Governor of Yizhou and Left Worthy King.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Huangshi era, Lu Guang appointed Wugu Governor of Yizhou and Left Worthy King.

sentences.zh: 烏孤私署大都督、大將軍、大單于、西平王，年號太初。

translations.literal: Wugu privately styled himself Grand Commander-in-Chief, Grand General, Grand Chanyu, and King of Xiping, with the era name Taichu.
translations.idiomatic: Wugu styled himself Grand Commander-in-Chief, Grand General, Grand Chanyu, and King of Xiping, adopting the era name Taichu.

sentences.zh: 天興初，烏孤又稱武威王，徙治樂都，置車騎將軍已下，分立郡縣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianxing, Wugu again styled himself King of Wuwei, moved his seat to Ledu, appointed officials down to General of Chariots and Cavalry, and established separate commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianxing era, Wugu styled himself King of Wuwei, moved his capital to Ledu, appointed officials down to General of Chariots and Cavalry, and established commanderies and counties.

sentences.zh: 烏孤因酒走馬，馬倒傷脅，笑曰：「幾為呂光父子所喜。」

translations.literal: Wugu, drunk, galloped his horse; the horse fell and injured his flank. He laughed and said: "I nearly gave Lu Guang and his son something to celebrate."
translations.idiomatic: While drunk, Wugu galloped his horse; it stumbled and injured his flank. He laughed and said: "I nearly gave Lu Guang and his son reason to rejoice."

sentences.zh: 既而遂死。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he died.

sentences.zh: 弟涼州牧、西平公利鹿孤統任，徙治西平，改年建和。

translations.literal: His younger brother Lilugu, Governor of Liangzhou and Duke of Xiping, succeeded to the command, moved the seat to Xiping, and changed the era name to Jianhe.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Lilugu, Governor of Liangzhou and Duke of Xiping, took over leadership, moved the capital to Xiping, and adopted the era name Jianhe.

sentences.zh: 使使朝貢。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to pay court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to pay tribute at court.

sentences.zh: 遣弟車騎將軍傉檀拒呂纂，纂士馬精銳，軍人大懼，傉檀下馬據胡牀，以安眾情。

translations.literal: He sent his younger brother Rutan, General of Chariots and Cavalry, to resist Lu Zuan. Zuan's troops and horses were elite and sharp; the soldiers were greatly afraid. Rutan dismounted and sat on a folding camp chair to steady the troops' spirits.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched his younger brother Rutan, General of Chariots and Cavalry, to resist Lu Zuan. Zuan's forces were crack troops, and the army was terrified. Rutan dismounted and seated himself on a folding camp chair to calm them.

sentences.zh: 乃貫甲交戰，破纂軍，斬二千餘級。

translations.literal: Then, fully armored, they joined battle, broke Zuan's army, and beheaded more than two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: They then fought in full armor, routed Zuan's army, and killed more than two thousand men.

sentences.zh: [7]利鹿孤私署百官，自丞相以下。

translations.literal: [7] Lilugu privately appointed the hundred officials, from the Chancellor downward.
translations.idiomatic: [7] Lilugu established his own bureaucracy, appointing officials from the Chancellor on down.

sentences.zh: 利鹿孤死，傉檀統任，私署涼王。

translations.literal: When Lilugu died, Rutan succeeded to the command and privately styled himself King of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: After Lilugu's death, Rutan took over leadership and styled himself King of Liang.

sentences.zh: 還居樂都，年號洪昌。

translations.literal: He returned to dwell at Ledu, with the era name Hongchang.
translations.idiomatic: He moved back to Ledu and adopted the era name Hongchang.

sentences.zh: 遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to pay court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to pay tribute at court.

sentences.zh: 天賜中，傉檀詐降姚興，興以傉檀為涼州刺史，遂據姑臧。

translations.literal: During Tianci, Rutan feigned submission to Yao Xing; Xing made Rutan Inspector of Liangzhou, and Rutan then seized Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianci era, Rutan feigned submission to Yao Xing, who appointed him Inspector of Liangzhou; Rutan then seized Guzang.

sentences.zh: 與沮渠蒙遜戰於均石，為蒙遜所敗。

translations.literal: He fought Juqu Mengxun at Junshi and was defeated by Mengxun.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Juqu Mengxun at Junshi and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 傉檀又為赫連屈丐所破於陽武，以數千騎奔南山，幾為追騎所得。

translations.literal: Rutan was again defeated by Helian Quke at Yangwu; with several thousand horsemen he fled to Nanshan and was nearly captured by pursuing cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan was defeated again by Helian Quke at Yangwu and fled south with several thousand horsemen, barely escaping the pursuing cavalry.

sentences.zh: 懼東西寇至，乃徙三百里內民於姑臧。

translations.literal: Fearing enemies from east and west, he then moved the people within three hundred li into Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing attack from both east and west, he relocated the population within three hundred li into Guzang.

sentences.zh: 姚興乘釁遣將姚弼等至於城下，傉檀驅牛羊於野，弼眾採掠，傉檀因分擊大破之，弼乃退還。

translations.literal: Yao Xing seized the opportunity and sent the generals Yao Bi and others to the foot of the city. Rutan drove cattle and sheep into the open country; Bi's troops went out to plunder, and Rutan then divided his forces, struck, and routed them greatly; Bi then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing seized the moment and sent Yao Bi and others to the city walls. Rutan drove cattle and sheep into the open fields; when Bi's men went out to plunder, Rutan divided his forces, struck, and routed them; Bi then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 傉檀又自署涼王，署百官，改號嘉平。

translations.literal: Rutan again styled himself King of Liang, appointed the hundred officials, and changed the reign title to Jiaping.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan again styled himself King of Liang, established a full court, and adopted the reign title Jiaping.

sentences.zh: 永興中，盡眾伐沮渠蒙遜，為蒙遜所敗於窮泉，單馬歸姑臧。

translations.literal: During Yongxing he led all his forces to attack Juqu Mengxun and was defeated by Mengxun at Qiongquan; he returned to Guzang alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongxing era he marched against Juqu Mengxun with his full army, was defeated at Qiongquan, and rode back to Guzang alone.

sentences.zh: 懼為蒙遜所滅，[8]乃遷于樂都。

translations.literal: Fearing destruction by Mengxun, [8] he then moved to Ledu.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing annihilation by Mengxun, [8] he relocated to Ledu.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜以兵圍之，築室反耕，為持久之計。

translations.literal: Mengxun besieged it with troops, built houses, and turned the soil for planting, making plans for a prolonged siege.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun besieged the city, built houses, and planted fields—preparing for a long campaign.

sentences.zh: 傉檀以子保周為質於蒙遜，蒙遜乃還。

translations.literal: Rutan sent his son Baozhou as hostage to Mengxun, and Mengxun then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Rutan sent his son Baozhou as a hostage to Mengxun, who then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 神瑞初，傉檀率騎擊乙弗虜，大有擒獲，而乞伏熾磐乘虛襲樂都克之，執傉檀子虎臺以下。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenrui, Rutan led cavalry to attack the Yifu barbarians and took many captives; meanwhile Qifu Chipan seized the opportunity, raided Ledu, captured it, and seized Rutan's son Hutai and those below him.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Shenrui era, Rutan led cavalry against the Yifu tribes and took many captives; meanwhile Qifu Chipan seized the moment, struck Ledu, captured it, and took Rutan's son Hutai and his household.

sentences.zh: 傉檀聞之曰：「若歸熾磐，便為奴僕，豈忍見妻子在他懷中也！」

translations.literal: When Rutan heard this he said: "If I submit to Chipan, I become a slave—how could I bear to see my wife and children in another man's arms!"
translations.idiomatic: When Rutan heard the news he said: "If I submit to Chipan I become a slave—how could I bear to see my wife and children in another man's arms!"

sentences.zh: 引眾而西，眾皆離散。

translations.literal: He led his followers westward, and the followers all dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: He led his followers westward, but they all deserted him.

sentences.zh: 傉檀曰：「蒙遜、熾磐昔皆委質於吾，今而歸之，不亦鄙哉！

translations.literal: Rutan said: "Mengxun and Chipan both once sent hostages to me; to submit to them now—would that not be contemptible!
translations.idiomatic: Rutan said: "Mengxun and Chipan both once sent hostages to me—how shameful to submit to them now!

sentences.zh: 四海之廣，無所容身，何其痛乎！」

translations.literal: The four seas are vast, yet there is nowhere to shelter my body—how painful!"
translations.idiomatic: All the world is wide, yet nowhere will have me—how bitter!"

sentences.zh: 既乃歎曰：「吾老矣，寧見妻子而死。」

translations.literal: Then he sighed and said: "I am old; I would rather see my wife and children and die."
translations.idiomatic: He sighed and said: "I am old—I would rather see my wife and children one last time and die."

sentences.zh: 遂降熾磐，熾磐待以上賓之禮，用為驃騎大將軍，封左南公。

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted to Chipan. Chipan treated him with the rites due a highest guest, employed him as General of Agile Cavalry, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Zuonan.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted to Chipan, who received him with the honors due a distinguished guest, appointed him General of Agile Cavalry, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Zuonan.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，鴆殺之。

translations.literal: After more than a year, Chipan poisoned him to death.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later, Chipan had him poisoned.

sentences.zh: 傉檀少子賀，後來奔，自有傳。

translations.literal: Rutan's youngest son He later came and surrendered; there is a separate biography [for him].
translations.idiomatic: Rutan's youngest son, He, later came and submitted; his biography is given separately.

sentences.zh: 李暠，字玄盛，小字長生，隴西狄道人也，漢前將軍廣之後。

translations.literal: Li Gao, style name Xuansheng, childhood name Changsheng, was a native of Didao in Longxi; he was a descendant of Guang, General of the Vanguard of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gao, styled Xuansheng and known in youth as Changsheng, was a native of Didao in Longxi and a descendant of Li Guang, Han's General of the Vanguard.

sentences.zh: 曾祖柔，晉相國從事中郎、北地太守。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Rou was Attendant Officer in the Chancellor's Office of Jin and Administrator of Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Rou served Jin as Attendant Officer in the Chancellor's Office and as Administrator of Beidi.

sentences.zh: 祖太，張祚武衞將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tai [9] was General of Martial Guard under Zhang Zuo.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tai [9] served as General of Martial Guard under Zhang Zuo.

sentences.zh: 父昶，早卒，暠，遺腹子也。

translations.literal: His father Chang died early; Gao was a posthumous son.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chang died young, and Gao was born after his death.

sentences.zh: 皇始中，呂光建康太守段業自稱涼州牧，以敦煌太守孟敏為沙州刺史，暠為效穀令。

translations.literal: In the Huangshi era, Duan Ye, Administrator of Jiankang under Lü Guang, styled himself Governor of Liangzhou; he appointed Meng Min, Administrator of Dunhuang, as Inspector of Shazhou, and Gao as Magistrate of Xiaogu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huangshi reign, Duan Ye, Administrator of Jiankang under Lü Guang, proclaimed himself Governor of Liangzhou, appointed Meng Min of Dunhuang as Inspector of Shazhou, and made Gao magistrate of Xiaogu.

sentences.zh: 敏死，敦煌護軍郭謙等推暠為寧朔將軍、敦煌太守。

translations.literal: When Min died, Guo Qian of the Dunhuang Protectorate and others urged Gao [to take office] as General Who Pacifies the North and Administrator of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: After Min's death, Guo Qian and other officers of the Dunhuang Protectorate installed Gao as General Who Pacifies the North and Administrator of Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 業私稱涼王，暠詐臣於業，業以暠為鎮西將軍。

translations.literal: Ye privately styled himself King of Liang; Gao pretended to submit to Ye, and Ye made Gao General Who Guards the West.
translations.idiomatic: When Duan Ye took the title King of Liang on his own authority, Gao feigned allegiance to him and was appointed General Who Guards the West.

sentences.zh: 天興中，暠私署大都督、大將軍、護羌校尉、秦涼二州牧、涼公，年號庚子，居敦煌，遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the Tianxing era, Gao privately appointed himself Grand Commander, Grand General, Protector of the Qiang, Governor of the two provinces Qin and Liang, and Duke of Liang; his reign title was Gengzi; he resided at Dunhuang and sent envoys to pay court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianxing reign, Gao took the titles Grand Commander, Grand General, Protector of the Qiang, Governor of Qin and Liang, and Duke of Liang; he adopted the reign era Gengzi, made Dunhuang his seat, and sent tribute missions to court.

sentences.zh: 天賜中，改年建初，遷於酒泉，歲修職貢。

translations.literal: In the Tianci era, he changed the era to Jianchu, moved to Jiuquan, and every year maintained tribute duties.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianci he changed his era name to Jianchu, moved his capital to Jiuquan, and continued to send annual tribute.

sentences.zh: 暠死，子歆統任。

translations.literal: When Gao died, his son Xin succeeded to the command.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Gao died, his son Xin succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 歆，字士業，自稱大都督、大將軍、護羌校尉、涼州牧、涼公，號年嘉興元年。

translations.literal: Xin, style name Shuye, styled himself Grand Commander, Grand General, Protector of the Qiang, Governor of Liangzhou, and Duke of Liang; his reign title was the first year of Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: Xin, styled Shuye, assumed the titles Grand Commander, Grand General, Protector of the Qiang, Governor of Liangzhou, and Duke of Liang, and proclaimed the first year of his Jiaxing era.

sentences.zh: 大破沮渠蒙遜於鮮支澗，獲七千餘級。

translations.literal: He utterly defeated Juqu Mengxun at Xianzhi Stream [10], capturing more than seven thousand [enemy heads].
translations.idiomatic: He won a crushing victory over Juqu Mengxun at Xianzhi Stream [10], taking more than seven thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to pay court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched envoys with tribute to the court.

sentences.zh: 歆聞蒙遜南伐乞伏，乃起兵攻張掖。

translations.literal: When Xin heard that Mengxun was campaigning south against the Qifu, he raised troops and attacked Zhangye.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Mengxun had marched south against the Qifu, Xin mobilized an army to strike at Zhangye.

sentences.zh: 其母尹氏謂歆曰：「汝新造之國，地狹民希，蒙遜驍武，汝非其敵。

translations.literal: His mother, Lady Yin, said to Xin: "Your state is newly founded; its territory is narrow and its people few. Mengxun is fierce and martial—you are no match for him.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Yin, warned Xin: "You have only just established your realm—small in land and thin in population. Mengxun is a formidable warrior, and you cannot stand against him.

sentences.zh: 吾觀其數年以來，經謀規略，有兼并之志，且天時人事，似欲歸之。

translations.literal: I have observed that over these several years his stratagems and plans show a desire to annex [territory], and both the times and men's hearts seem inclined to go to him.
translations.idiomatic: I have watched him for years—every plan he makes aims at conquest, and both Heaven and men seem ready to rally to him.

sentences.zh: 度德量力，春秋之義。

translations.literal: Measuring virtue and gauging strength—this is the principle of the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: To weigh one's virtue against another's and measure one's strength against his—that is the teaching of the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 先王遺令『深慎兵戰，保境寧民，俟時而動』，言猶在耳，奈何忘之。

translations.literal: The late king's final charge—"deeply beware of warfare, keep the borders secure and the people at peace, and wait for the right moment to act"—is still ringing in my ears; how can you forget it?
translations.idiomatic: Your father's last injunction—"be deeply cautious of war, keep the realm peaceful, and act only when the time is ripe"—still rings in my ears. How can you cast it aside?

sentences.zh: 汝必行也，非唯師敗，國亦亡矣。」

translations.literal: If you insist on going, not only will the army be defeated—the state will also perish."
translations.idiomatic: If you go through with this, you will not merely lose the battle—you will lose the kingdom."

sentences.zh: 歆不從，遂率步騎三萬東伐，次于都瀆澗。

translations.literal: Xin did not listen; he then led thirty thousand infantry and cavalry on an eastern campaign and encamped at Dudugou Stream.
translations.idiomatic: Xin would not be persuaded. He led thirty thousand foot and horse eastward and halted at Dudugou Stream.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜自浩舋拒歆，戰于懷城，為蒙遜所敗。

translations.literal: Mengxun came out from Haofan to oppose Xin; they fought at Huaicheng, and Xin was defeated by Mengxun.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun marched from Haofan to meet him. They fought at Huaicheng, and Xin was routed.

sentences.zh: 左右勸歆還酒泉，歆曰：「吾違太后明敕，遠取敗辱，不殺此胡，復何面目見吾母也！」

translations.literal: Those around him urged Xin to return to Jiuquan. Xin said: "I defied the Empress Dowager's clear command and suffered defeat far from home. If I do not kill this barbarian, with what face can I meet my mother?"
translations.idiomatic: His attendants urged him to fall back to Jiuquan, but Xin said: "I ignored my mother's wise counsel and came to grief in this distant field. If I do not kill that barbarian, how can I face my mother again?"

sentences.zh: 勒眾復戰，敗于蓼泉，為蒙遜所殺，蒙遜遂克酒泉。

translations.literal: He drove his troops to battle again, was defeated at Liaoyuan, was killed by Mengxun, and Mengxun thereupon captured Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied his men for another fight, was defeated at Liaoyuan, and was killed by Mengxun, who then took Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 歆之未敗，有一大蛇從南門而入，至歆恭德殿前，有雙雉飛出；

translations.literal: Before Xin's defeat, a great serpent entered through the south gate and came before the Gongde Hall; a pair of pheasants flew out.
translations.idiomatic: Before Xin fell, an enormous serpent slithered in through the south gate as far as the Gongde Hall, and two pheasants flew out from within.

sentences.zh: 宮內通街大樹上有烏鵲爭巢，鵲為烏所殺。

translations.literal: On a great tree in the palace's main thoroughfare, crows and magpies fought over a nest, and the magpies were killed by the crows.
translations.idiomatic: On a large tree in the palace avenue, crows and magpies fought over a nest, and the crows killed the magpies.

sentences.zh: 敦煌父老令狐熾夢一白頭公帢衣，而謂曰：「南風動，吹長木。

translations.literal: Linghu Chi, an elder of Dunhuang, dreamed of a white-haired old man in a headcloth and robe who said to him: "The south wind stirs, blowing the tall tree.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Chi, a leading citizen of Dunhuang, dreamed of a white-haired old man in cap and robe who said to him: "When the south wind rises, it will blow down the tall tree.

sentences.zh: 胡桐椎，不中轂。」

translations.literal: The foreign Tongzhui will not even reach the hub."
translations.idiomatic: The barbarian and Tongzhui—the axle hub itself will not be spared."

sentences.zh: 言訖，忽然不見。

translations.literal: When he finished speaking, he suddenly vanished.
translations.idiomatic: When he had finished speaking, the figure vanished without warning.

sentences.zh: 歆小字桐椎，至是而亡。

translations.literal: Xin's childhood name was Tongzhui; at this point he perished.
translations.idiomatic: Xin's childhood name was Tongzhui—and at this time he met his end, just as the prophecy foretold.

sentences.zh: 歆弟敦煌太守恂復自立于敦煌，稱冠軍將軍、涼州刺史。

translations.literal: Xin's younger brother Xun, Administrator of Dunhuang, again established himself at Dunhuang and styled himself General Who Crowns the Army and Inspector of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xin's younger brother Xun, who held Dunhuang, set himself up there again as General Who Crowns the Army and Inspector of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜攻恂于敦煌，三面起堤，以水灌城。

translations.literal: Mengxun attacked Xun at Dunhuang, raised dikes on three sides, and flooded the city with water.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun besieged Xun at Dunhuang, building embankments on three sides to inundate the city.

sentences.zh: 恂請降，不許。

translations.literal: Xun requested surrender; [Mengxun] would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Xun offered to surrender, but Mengxun refused.

sentences.zh: 城陷，恂自殺，蒙遜克敦煌。

translations.literal: When the city fell, Xun killed himself, and Mengxun captured Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Xun took his own life, and Mengxun seized Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 恂兄翻子寶後入國，自有傳。

translations.literal: Bao, son of Xun's elder brother Fan, later entered [Wei]; there is a separate biography [for him].
translations.idiomatic: Bao, nephew of Xun through his elder brother Fan, later came to the Northern Wei court; his biography is given separately.

sentences.zh: 永興中，蒙遜克姑臧，遷居之。

translations.literal: In the Yongxing era, Mengxun captured Guzang and moved his seat there.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongxing, Mengxun took Guzang and transferred his capital there.

sentences.zh: 改號玄始元年，自稱河西王，置百官丞郎以下，頻遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: He changed his reign title to the first year of Xuanshi, styled himself King of Hexi, established the full bureaucracy down to Assistant Grand Clerks, and frequently sent envoys to pay court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed the Xuanshi era, took the title King of Hexi, installed a full court down to assistant clerks, and sent tribute missions again and again.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜寢於新臺，閹人王懷祖斫蒙遜傷足，蒙遜妻孟氏擒懷祖斬之。

translations.literal: While Mengxun was sleeping on the New Terrace, the eunuch Wang Huaizu hacked at Mengxun and wounded his foot; Mengxun's wife Lady Meng seized Huaizu and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: While Mengxun slept on the New Terrace, the eunuch Wang Huaizu struck at him and wounded his foot. Mengxun's wife Lady Meng seized the assailant and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜聞劉裕滅姚泓，怒甚，有校書郎言事於蒙遜，蒙遜曰：「汝聞劉裕入關，敢妍妍然也！」

translations.literal: When Mengxun heard that Liu Yu had destroyed Yao Hong, he was greatly angered. A collation secretary reported some matter to Mengxun, and Mengxun said: "You heard that Liu Yu entered the Pass—how dare you prattle on so gleefully!"
translations.idiomatic: When Mengxun learned that Liu Yu had overthrown Yao Hong, he flew into a rage. A collation secretary spoke to him on some matter, and Mengxun snapped: "You heard Liu Yu enter the Pass—and you still prattle on as if pleased about it!"

sentences.zh: 遂殺之，其峻暴如此。

translations.literal: He thereupon killed him—so harsh and violent was he.
translations.idiomatic: He had the man killed on the spot—such was his savage temper.

sentences.zh: 泰常中，蒙遜克李歆，尋滅敦煌。

translations.literal: In the Taichang era, Mengxun defeated Li Xin; soon after he destroyed Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: During Taichang, Mengxun defeated Li Xin and soon afterward extinguished Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 後改年承玄。

translations.literal: Later he changed the era to Chengxuan.
translations.idiomatic: He later adopted the Chengxuan era.

sentences.zh: 神䴥中，遣尚書郎宗舒、左常侍高猛朝貢，上表曰：「伏惟陛下天縱叡聖，德超百王，陶育齊於二儀，洪基隆於三代。

translations.literal: In the Shenjuan era, he sent Minister Lang Zong Shu and Left Attendant-in-Ordinary Gao Meng to pay court tribute; they submitted a memorial saying: "We bow before Your Majesty's Heaven-given sagacity and wisdom, virtue surpassing the hundred kings, nurturing equal to the Two Principles, and grand foundation loftier than the Three Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: During Shenjuan, he dispatched Zong Shu of the Secretariat and Gao Meng, Left Attendant-in-Ordinary, with tribute; their memorial read: "We bow before Your Majesty—endowed by Heaven with sagely wisdom, your virtue exceeds that of the hundred kings; your nurturing reach matches heaven and earth, and your foundation towers above the Three Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 然鍾運多難，九服紛擾，神旗暫擁，車書未同。

translations.literal: Yet the age was struck by many tribulations; the nine domains were in turmoil; the divine banner was for a time unfurled, but chariots and writing were not yet unified.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the times were vexed by manifold disasters; all under heaven was in disorder; though the banner of rule was raised, the realm had not yet been brought under one chariot and one script.

sentences.zh: 上靈降祐，祚歸有道，純風一鼓，殊方革面。

translations.literal: The Supreme Spirits sent down blessing; the mandate returned to the one possessed of the Way; at one blast of pure virtue, distant regions changed their faces.
