translations.idiomatic: The divine powers bestowed their blessing; the mandate fell to the rightful ruler; at a single breath of upright governance, distant lands turned their faces toward the center.

sentences.zh: 羣生幸甚，率土齊欣。

translations.literal: All living beings were most fortunate; throughout the land all rejoiced together.
translations.idiomatic: All creatures were blessed; the whole empire rejoiced as one.

sentences.zh: 臣誠弱才，效無可錄，幸遇重光，思竭力命。

translations.literal: Your subject is truly of meager talent, with achievements worth no record; yet having fortunately encountered renewed glory, I wish to exhaust my life in service.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject is truly without ability, his deeds unworthy of note—yet now that enlightened rule has returned, he wishes to give his utmost.

sentences.zh: 自欣投老，得覩盛化；

translations.literal: I rejoice that in my old age I have been able to behold this flourishing transformation;
translations.idiomatic: In my declining years I rejoice to have witnessed this age of flourishing rule;

sentences.zh: 冀終餘年，憑倚皇極。

translations.literal: I hope to end my remaining years leaning upon the imperial polestar.
translations.idiomatic: and I hope to spend my last years under the shelter of the imperial throne.

sentences.zh: 前後奉表，貢使相望，去者杳然，寂無旋返。

translations.literal: Memorials were submitted before and after; tribute envoys followed one upon another; those who departed vanished into the distance, and not one returned.
translations.idiomatic: Memorial after memorial we have sent; tribute missions went out one after another—yet those who departed disappeared into the distance, and not one returned.

sentences.zh: 未審津塗寇險，竟不仰達，為天朝高遠，未蒙齒錄？

translations.literal: We do not know whether the routes and fords were perilous with bandits and so our words failed to reach you—or whether the Heavenly Court is too remote and we have not been enrolled among its subjects?
translations.idiomatic: We cannot tell whether brigands blocked the roads and our words never reached you, or whether the Celestial Court, so far away, has simply not deigned to acknowledge us.

sentences.zh: 屏營戰灼，無地自措。

translations.literal: Anxiously we tremble and burn; there is no place to set ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: We tremble with anxiety and burn with shame, with nowhere to hide our faces.

sentences.zh: 往年侍郎郭祇等還，奉被詔書，三接之恩始隆，萬里之心有賴。

translations.literal: In past years Vice Minister Guo Qi and others returned and received your edict; the grace of three audiences was first extended, and hearts ten thousand li away had something to rely upon.
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Minister Guo Qi and his party returned last year bearing your edict, the grace of repeated audiences restored our hope, and hearts ten thousand leagues distant finally had something to hold to.

sentences.zh: 今極難之餘，開泰唯始，誘勸既加，引納彌篤。

translations.literal: Now, at the end of utmost hardship, great peace has just begun; encouragement and persuasion have been added, and your welcoming embrace grows ever deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Now, with the worst behind us and a new age opening, your encouragement grows ever warmer and your welcome ever more generous.

sentences.zh: 老臣見存，遐外無棄，仰荷愷悌之仁，俯蹈康哉之詠。

translations.literal: This aged minister is still preserved; the far frontier is not cast aside. We look up and bear your kind benevolence; we bow down and tread upon the song "How grand!"
translations.idiomatic: That you have kept this old minister alive and not abandoned us at the frontier's edge—we bear your generous kindness aloft and humbly echo the hymn "How glorious is your rule!"

sentences.zh: 然商胡後至，奉公卿書，援引歷數安危之機，厲以竇融知命之美。

translations.literal: Yet the merchant from the west arrived later, bearing a letter from your high ministers, citing the turning points of dynastic fortune in safety and danger, and pressing upon us the example of Dou Rong's beauty in knowing the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Then a western merchant arrived with a letter from your ministers, invoking the turning points of dynastic fortune and urging us to follow the example of Dou Rong, who knew when to align with the rightful power.

sentences.zh: 顧惟情願，實深悚惕。

translations.literal: Reflecting on my heartfelt wish, I am truly deeply fearful and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Yet as I weigh my own heartfelt wish, I am deeply apprehensive.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this?

sentences.zh: 臣不自揆，遠託大蔭，庶微誠上宣，天鑒下降。

translations.literal: Your subject does not measure himself, but entrusts himself from afar to your great shade, hoping that his slight sincerity may rise to announce itself and that Heaven's inspection may descend.
translations.idiomatic: Without presuming on my own worth, I have from afar placed myself under your great protection, hoping my humble sincerity might reach you and Heaven's judgment might look upon me with favor.

sentences.zh: 若萬國來庭，百辟陛賀，高蹈先至之端，獨步知機之首。

translations.literal: If all the myriad states come to court and the hundred ministers congratulate at the palace steps, I would tread foremost in arriving early and walk alone at the head of those who know the moment.
translations.idiomatic: When all states come to court and all ministers offer congratulations, I would be the first to arrive and foremost among those who know when the moment has come.

sentences.zh: 但世難尚殷，情願未遂，章表頻修，滯懷不暢，許身於國，款誠莫表。

translations.literal: But worldly troubles are still severe; my heartfelt wish has not been fulfilled; memorials have been frequently drafted yet my pent-up feelings cannot be released; I would devote my person to the state, but my earnest sincerity cannot be expressed.
translations.idiomatic: But troubles still abound, my wish remains unfulfilled, and though I send memorial after memorial my pent-up feelings cannot be released—I would give myself wholly to the state, yet have no way to show my full sincerity.

sentences.zh: 致惑羣后，貽慮公卿，辭旨紛紜，抑引重沓，不在同奬之例，未達拱辰之心，延首一隅，低回四極。

translations.literal: This has caused confusion among the feudal lords and concern among the ministers; the words and intent are tangled, praise and blame overlap repeatedly; I am not within the category of joint reward; I have not reached the heart of revolving around the polestar; I stretch my neck in one corner and look back and forth toward the four extremes.
translations.idiomatic: This has puzzled the feudal lords and troubled your ministers—the wording ambiguous, praise and restraint piled upon one another. I have not received the same rewards as others, nor have I fulfilled the duty of circling the polestar. I crane my neck from my remote corner and gaze longingly in every direction toward the center.

sentences.zh: 臣歷觀符瑞，候察天時，未有過於皇魏，踰於陛下。

translations.literal: Your subject has repeatedly observed portents and examined the signs of Heaven; none surpass Great Wei, nor any surpass Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: I have watched the portents and read the signs of Heaven, and I find none greater than the Northern Wei—none greater than Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 加以靈啟聖姿，幼登天位，美詠侔於成康，道化踰於文景。

translations.literal: Added to this are spiritual enlightenment and sagely mien; ascending the throne while still young; praises of beauty comparable to Cheng and Kang; the transforming power of the Way surpassing Wen and Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Endowed with sage wisdom, you ascended the throne while still young—your praise equals that of Kings Cheng and Kang, and your transforming influence surpasses Emperors Wen and Jing of Han.

sentences.zh: 方將振神綱以掩六合，灑玄澤以潤八荒。

translations.literal: You are about to raise the divine net to cover the six quarters and spread mysterious grace to moisten the eight wastes.
translations.idiomatic: You are about to extend the divine net over all six directions and pour forth your grace to enrich the farthest reaches of the earth.

sentences.zh: 況在秦隴荼炭之餘，直是老臣盡效之會。」

translations.literal: How much more so in Qin and Long, after scorch and ruin—this is precisely the moment for this aged minister to give his fullest service."
translations.idiomatic: And here in Qin and Long, lands still scarred by fire and sword, this is precisely the moment for an old minister like me to give everything he has."

sentences.zh: 後蒙遜遣子安周內侍，世祖遣兼太常李順持節拜蒙遜為假節，加侍中，都督涼州、西域羌戎諸軍事，太傅，行征西大將軍，涼州牧，涼王。

translations.literal: Later Mengxun sent his son Anzhou as inner attendant; Emperor Shizu dispatched Acting Grand Minister of Ceremonies Li Shun bearing the credentials of authority to invest Mengxun as Acting Bearer of the Staff of Authority, additionally appointed Attendant-in-Chief, Commander of all military affairs in Liangzhou, the Western Regions, and the Qiang and Rong, Grand Preceptor, Acting Grand General Who Expands the West, Governor of Liangzhou, and King of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Later Mengxun sent his son Anzhou to serve at court as a hostage, and Emperor Shizu dispatched Li Shun, Acting Grand Minister of Ceremonies, with credentials of authority to invest Mengxun as King of Liang—with concurrent appointments as Acting Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Attendant-in-Chief, Commander of military affairs in Liangzhou, the Western Regions, and the Qiang and Rong territories, Grand Preceptor, Acting Grand General Who Expands the West, and Governor of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 冊曰：「昔我皇祖冑自黃軒，總御羣才，攝服戎夏，疊曜重光，不殞其舊。

translations.literal: The investiture edict said: "In antiquity our imperial ancestors sprang from the Yellow Emperor; they gathered and governed all talents, brought the barbarians and Hua under control, and layered glory upon glory without losing their old inheritance.
translations.idiomatic: The investiture edict read: "From the Yellow Emperor our royal line descended; our forebears gathered all worthy men, subdued barbarian and Chinese alike, and passed down layered glory without end.

sentences.zh: 逮于太祖，應期協運，大業唯新，奄有區宇，受命作魏。

translations.literal: Reaching the Grand Ancestor, he answered the times and harmonized with the mandate; the great enterprise was wholly renewed; he embraced all within the four seas and received the mandate to establish Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Ancestor rose, he matched the age and answered Heaven's call, renewing the great enterprise, taking all within the four seas, and receiving the mandate to found Wei.

sentences.zh: 降及太宗，廣闢崇基，政和民阜。

translations.literal: Descending to the Grand Emperor [Taizong], he broadly opened and raised the foundation; government was harmonious and the people prosperous.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Emperor broadened and deepened that foundation until governance was harmonious and the people flourished.

sentences.zh: 朕承天緒，思廓宇縣，然時運或否，雰霧四張，赫連跋扈於關西，大檀陸梁於漠北，戎夷負阻，江淮未賓，是用自東徂西，戎軒屢駕。

translations.literal: We have inherited Heaven's thread and wish to extend the realm; yet times sometimes turn adverse, and mists spread on four sides—Helian Bao is overbearing in Guanxi and Datan runs riot north of the desert; barbarians cling to obstacles, and the Yangtze and Huai have not submitted. Therefore from east to west We have repeatedly driven Our military chariot.
translations.idiomatic: We have inherited Heaven's mandate and seek to bring all under heaven to order, yet fortune has not always favored us—mists rose on every side. Helian Bao ran rampant in Guanxi, Datan stirred trouble on the northern steppe, barbarians held the passes, and the Yangtze and Huai still held aloof. That is why We have driven Our war chariot again and again from east to west.

sentences.zh: 賴宗廟靈長，將士宣力，克翦兇渠，震服強獷，四方漸泰，表裏無塵。

translations.literal: Relying on the enduring spirit of the ancestral temple, with officers and soldiers exerting their strength, We cut down the vicious leaders and shook the mighty into submission; the four directions gradually grew peaceful, and inside and out were without dust.
translations.idiomatic: By the enduring blessing of our ancestors and the exertions of our officers and men, We cut down the wicked and awed the fierce into submission. Gradually the four quarters grew peaceful, and within and without all was calm.

sentences.zh: 王先識機運，經略深遠，與朕協同，厥功洪茂。

translations.literal: Your Majesty first discerned the turn of fortune; your plans were far-reaching; together with Us you acted in concert—your merit is vast and flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: You, O King, read the turning of fortune early and plotted with far-sighted strategy. Acting in concert with Us, your achievements have been great indeed.

sentences.zh: 當今運鍾時季，僭逆憑陵，有土者莫不跨峙一隅，有民者莫不榮其私號，不遵眾星拱極之道，不慕細流歸海之義。

translations.literal: In the present age the times strike at a declining season; usurpers and rebels rely on force and encroach; whoever holds land does not fail to straddle one corner; whoever holds people does not fail to glorify his private title—not following the Way of the myriad stars revolving around the pole, not cherishing the principle of tiny streams returning to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: The times are troubled: rebels and usurpers press their advantage. Every lord who holds land fortifies his corner; every ruler who commands men honors his own title—forgetting that stars must revolve around the pole and streams must flow back to the sea.

sentences.zh: 而王深悟大體，率由典章，任土貢珍，愛子入侍。

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty deeply comprehends the great principle, follows the statutes and ordinances, sends tribute according to your land's products, and sends your beloved son to attend at court.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you, O King, have grasped the larger truth, followed our laws and precedents, sent tribute according to your land's produce, and offered your beloved son for service at court.

sentences.zh: 勳義著焉，道業存焉。

translations.literal: Meritorious righteousness is manifest therein; the Way and its work are preserved therein.
translations.idiomatic: Thus your merit and loyalty are made manifest, and the Way is upheld through your deeds.

sentences.zh: 惟王乃祖乃父有土有民，論功德則無二於當時，言氏族則始因於世爵。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's grandfathers and fathers possessed land and people; speaking of merit and virtue, they had no second in their time; speaking of clan lineage, they began by inheriting a hereditary enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Your forebears held land and commanded men; in merit none rivalled them in their day, and your house's standing began with a hereditary noble title.

sentences.zh: 古先帝王褒賢賞德，莫不胙土分民，建為藩輔，是以周成命太公以表東海，襄王錫晉文大啟南陽。

translations.literal: Ancient emperors and kings, in honoring the worthy and rewarding virtue, all without exception granted estates and divided out people, establishing [such men] as frontier supports. Thus King Cheng of Zhou commanded the Grand Duke to mark out the Eastern Sea, and King Xiang enfeoffed Duke Wen of Jin with a great opening of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity, emperors and kings who honored worth and rewarded virtue have granted lands and subjects and installed such men as frontier bulwarks—King Cheng of Zhou enfeoffed the Grand Duke on the Eastern Sea, and King Xiang of Zhou granted Duke Wen of Jin the great domain of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 是用割涼州之武威、張掖、敦煌、酒泉、西海、金城、西平七郡封王為涼王。

translations.literal: Therefore We cut from Liangzhou the seven commanderies Wuwei, Zhangye, Dunhuang, Jiuquan, Xihai, Jincheng, and Xiping and enfeoff Your Majesty as King of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore We carve out from Liangzhou the seven commanderies of Wuwei, Zhangye, Dunhuang, Jiuquan, Xihai, Jincheng, and Xiping and enfeoff you as King of Liang.

sentences.zh: 受茲素土，苴以白茅，用建冢社，為魏室藩輔，盛衰存亡，與魏升降。

translations.literal: Receive this pure earth, wrapped with white thatch, and use it to establish your ancestral altar; be a frontier support of the Wei house—rising and falling, surviving and perishing, together with Wei ascending and descending.
translations.idiomatic: Receive this sacred earth bound with white thatch, establish your ancestral shrine, and serve as a bulwark of the Wei house—your fortunes to rise and fall with Wei's own.

sentences.zh: 夫功高則爵尊，德厚則任重，又加命王入贊百揆，謀謨幃幄，出征不懷，登攝侯伯。

translations.literal: When merit is high, rank is exalted; when virtue is deep, responsibility is heavy. Further, We appoint Your Majesty to enter and assist in the hundred administrations, to plan strategy within the curtain, to set out on campaign without hesitation, and to ascend and oversee the marquises and earls.
translations.idiomatic: Great merit earns exalted rank; deep virtue carries heavy responsibility. We further appoint you to assist in state affairs, to counsel within the inner circle, to march without hesitation, and to oversee the frontier lords.

sentences.zh: 其以太傅行征西大將軍，仗鉞秉旄，鷹揚河右，遠祛王略，懷柔荒隅，北盡于窮髮，南極於庸岷，西被于崐嶺，東至于河曲，王實征之，以夾輔皇室。

translations.literal: Let him serve as Grand Preceptor and Acting Grand General Who Expands the West, bearing the battle-axe and holding the banner, soaring like a hawk over the lands west of the Yellow River, extending the kingly plan far abroad, cherishing and softening the wild frontiers—north to Qiongfa, south to Yongmin, west to Kunlun, east to the bend of the River. Your Majesty shall truly campaign therein to flank and support the imperial house.
translations.idiomatic: As Grand Preceptor and Acting Grand General Who Expands the West, bear the battle-axe and commander's banner and sweep like a hawk over the lands west of the River. Extend the royal design to distant borders and win over the wild frontiers—north to Qiongfa, south to Yong and Min, west to the Kunlun ranges, east to the River's bend. There you shall campaign in earnest to support the throne from the flank.

sentences.zh: 又命王建國：署將相羣卿百官，承制假授，除文官刺史以還、武官撫軍以下；

translations.literal: Further, We command Your Majesty to establish a state: appoint generals, chancellors, and all the hundred officials; receive Our mandate and provisionally grant appointments—civil officials from Inspector downward and military officials from General Who Pacifies the Army downward.
translations.idiomatic: We further authorize you to establish your own state, appointing generals, ministers, and all officials, and to grant provisional appointments on Our authority—for civil ranks from Inspector down and military ranks from General Who Pacifies the Army down.

sentences.zh: 建天子旌旗，出入警蹕，如漢初諸侯王故事。

translations.literal: Erect the imperial banners, with advance clearing of the road on going out and coming in, according to the precedent of the feudal kings in early Han.
translations.idiomatic: You may raise imperial banners and receive the road-clearing honors of the throne, as the feudal kings did in the early Han.

sentences.zh: 欽哉惟時，往踐乃職，祗服朕命，協亮天工，俾九德咸事，無忝庶官，用終爾顯德，對揚我皇祖之休烈。」

translations.literal: Reverently [receive this]—now is the time; go and perform your duties; respectfully obey Our command, harmoniously assist Heaven's work, cause the nine virtues all to be fulfilled, be not unworthy of the myriad offices, and thereby complete your illustrious virtue, responding to and proclaiming our imperial ancestors' glorious achievements."
translations.idiomatic: Reverence this charge. Go now and fulfill your duties. Obey Our command, aid Heaven's work in harmony, let all nine virtues be realized, disgrace none of your many offices, and so crown your noble virtue—proclaiming the glorious deeds of our imperial forebears."

sentences.zh: 崔浩之辭也。

translations.literal: This was the wording of Cui Hao.
translations.idiomatic: The edict was composed by Cui Hao.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜又改稱義和元年。

translations.literal: Mengxun again changed his reign title to the first year of Yihe.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun next proclaimed the first year of the Yihe era.

sentences.zh: 延和二年四月，蒙遜死，遣使監護喪事，諡曰武宣王。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Yanhe, Mengxun died; [Wei] dispatched envoys to oversee the funeral; his posthumous title was King Wu-Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Yanhe 2, Mengxun died. The court sent envoys to supervise the funeral and granted him the posthumous title King Wu-Xuan.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜性淫忌，忍於刑戮，閨庭之中，略無風禮。

translations.literal: Mengxun was by nature licentious and jealous, ruthless in punishment and execution; within the inner chambers there was scarcely any propriety of conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun was licentious and jealous by nature, merciless in punishment, and utterly devoid of decorum even within his own household.

sentences.zh: 第三子牧犍統任，自稱河西王，遣使請朝命。

translations.literal: His third son Mujian succeeded to the command, styled himself King of Hexi, and sent envoys to request court appointment.
translations.idiomatic: His third son Mujian succeeded him, took the title King of Hexi, and sent envoys to request formal recognition from the court.

sentences.zh: 太延五年，世祖遣尚書賀多羅使涼州，且觀虛實。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taiyan, Emperor Shizu dispatched Minister He Duoluo as envoy to Liangzhou to observe the actual situation.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiyan 5, Emperor Shizu sent Minister He Duoluo to Liangzhou to reconnoiter conditions there.

sentences.zh: 以牧犍雖稱蕃致貢，而內多乖悖，於是親征之。

translations.literal: Because although Mujian styled himself a vassal and sent tribute, inwardly he was greatly rebellious, [the Emperor] thereupon personally campaigned against him.
translations.idiomatic: Though Mujian professed vassalage and sent tribute, his conduct was deeply disloyal, and the Emperor marched against him in person.

sentences.zh: 詔公卿為書讓之曰：「王外從正朔，內不捨僭，罪一也。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the ministers to compose a letter of reproof saying: "Your Majesty outwardly follows the correct calendar, yet inwardly does not abandon usurpation—this is the first offense.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered his ministers to draw up a letter of rebuke: "You outwardly observe Our calendar yet inwardly cling to your usurped titles—this is your first offense.

sentences.zh: 民籍地圖不登公府，任土作貢，不入司農，罪二也。

translations.literal: Household registers and territorial maps are not submitted to the public offices; tribute according to the land's products does not enter the Minister of Revenue—this is the second offense.
translations.idiomatic: You have not submitted household registers and territorial maps to the imperial offices, nor sent tribute to the Ministry of Revenue as required—this is your second offense.

sentences.zh: 既荷王爵，又受偽官，取兩端之榮，邀不二之寵，罪三也。

translations.literal: Having received a royal enfeoffment, you also accept false offices, taking glory from both sides and seeking undivided favor from both—this is the third offense.
translations.idiomatic: Having received a royal enfeoffment from Us, you also accept offices from pretenders—seeking honor from both sides and undivided favor from two masters—this is your third offense.

sentences.zh: 知朝廷志在懷遠，固違聖略，切稅商胡，以斷行旅，罪四也。

translations.literal: Knowing the court's intent is to embrace the distant, you stubbornly violate the sacred strategy, heavily taxing merchant foreigners and thereby cutting off travelers—this is the fourth offense.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the court seeks to embrace distant peoples, you defy imperial policy, impose heavy levies on foreign merchants, and obstruct the roads—this is your fourth offense.

sentences.zh: 揚言西戎，高自驕大，罪五也。

translations.literal: You proclaim [your power] to the western Rong and hold yourself haughty and grand—this is the fifth offense.
translations.idiomatic: You boast to the western tribes and hold yourself insufferably proud—this is your fifth offense.

sentences.zh: 坐自封殖，不欲入朝，罪六也。

translations.literal: Resting on your self-enclosed growth, you do not wish to come to court—this is the sixth offense.
translations.idiomatic: Secure in your self-made domain, you refuse to attend court—this is your sixth offense.

sentences.zh: 北託叛虜，南引仇池，憑援谷軍，[12]提挈為姦，罪七也。

translations.literal: To the north you rely on rebel barbarians; to the south you draw in Chou Pool; depending on Gujun [12], you link together to commit treachery—this is the seventh offense.
translations.idiomatic: To the north you lean on rebel barbarians; to the south you court allies from Chouchi; you collude with Gujun [12] in treacherous schemes—this is your seventh offense.

sentences.zh: 承敕過限，輒假征、鎮，罪八也。

translations.literal: Exceeding the limits of received edicts, you presumptuously appoint expeditionary and garrison [generals]—this is the eighth offense.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond what Our edicts permit, you presumptuously appoint expeditionary and garrison commanders—this is your eighth offense.

sentences.zh: 欣敵之全，幸我之敗，侮慢王人，供不以禮，罪九也。

translations.literal: You rejoice in the enemy's completeness, hope for Our defeat, insult and slight the King's men, and supply them without proper ritual—this is the ninth offense.
translations.idiomatic: You rejoice when enemies prosper, pray for Our defeat, insult Our envoys, and treat them without due ceremony—this is your ninth offense.

sentences.zh: 既婚帝室，寵踰功舊，方恣慾情，蒸淫其嫂，罪十也。

translations.literal: Having married into the imperial house, your favor exceeded meritorious elders; you then indulged your lusts and committed incest with your sister-in-law—this is the tenth offense.
translations.idiomatic: Having married into the imperial clan, you enjoyed favor beyond what meritorious elders received; you gave free rein to your passions and committed incest with your sister-in-law—this is your tenth offense.

sentences.zh: 既違伉儷之體，不篤婚姻之義，公行酖毒，規害公主，罪十一也。

translations.literal: Having violated the propriety of husband and wife and failing in the obligations of marriage, you openly administered poisonous wine and plotted to harm the Princess—this is the eleventh offense.
translations.idiomatic: You violated the bond of marriage and betrayed its obligations, openly used poison, and plotted against the Princess—this is your eleventh offense.

sentences.zh: 備防王人，候守關要，有如寇讎，罪十二也。

translations.literal: You fortified defenses against the King's men and guarded strategic passes as though against bandits and enemies—this is the twelfth offense.
translations.idiomatic: You fortified your defenses against Our envoys and manned the strategic passes as though We were invaders—this is your twelfth offense.

sentences.zh: 為臣如是，其可恕乎！

translations.literal: As a subject behaving thus, can it be forgiven!
translations.idiomatic: Can such conduct from a vassal be forgiven!

sentences.zh: 先令後誅，王者之典也。

translations.literal: First to command, then to execute—this is the king's canonical practice.
translations.idiomatic: To issue warning before meting punishment is the sovereign's way.

sentences.zh: 若親率羣臣，委贄郊迎，謁拜馬首，上策也；

translations.literal: If you personally lead your ministers, surrender credentials in suburban welcome, and pay homage at the horse's head—this is the highest course;
translations.idiomatic: If you come in person at the head of your ministers, submit your credentials in ritual welcome outside the city, and bow before Our horse—this is the best course;

sentences.zh: 六軍既臨，面縛輿櫬，又其次也。

translations.literal: When the six armies have already arrived, to bind oneself with face covered and carry the coffin-wood—this is the next best.
translations.idiomatic: If Our six armies are already at your gates, binding yourself in surrender and bearing the coffin wood—this is the next best.

sentences.zh: 如其守迷窮城，不時悛悟，身死族滅，為世大戮。

translations.literal: If accordingly you hold a deluded, beleaguered city and do not repent in time, body death and clan extermination will make you a great object of ridicule for the world.
translations.idiomatic: If you cling obstinately to your doomed city and fail to repent in time, you and your clan will be destroyed and become a byword for generations.

sentences.zh: 宜思厥中，自求多福也。」

translations.literal: You ought to ponder the middle course and seek much fortune for yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Consider your course carefully, and may you find your own salvation."

sentences.zh: 官軍濟河，牧犍曰：「何故爾也！」

translations.literal: When the imperial army crossed the river, Mujian said: "Why is it thus!"
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army crossed the river, Mujian exclaimed, "What does this mean!

sentences.zh: 用其左丞姚定國計，不肯出迎，求救於蠕蠕，又遣弟董來率兵萬餘人拒官軍於城南，戰退。

translations.literal: He adopted the plan of his Left Chancellor Yao Dingguo, refused to come out in welcome, sought rescue from the Rouran, and also sent his younger brother Donglai leading more than ten thousand troops to oppose the imperial army south of the city; they fought and were driven back.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the advice of his Left Chancellor Yao Dingguo, refused to come out to welcome the army, appealed to the Rouran for aid, and sent his younger brother Donglai with more than ten thousand men to resist the imperial forces south of the city. They were defeated and driven back.

sentences.zh: 車駕至姑臧，遣使喻牧犍令出。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage reached Guzang, [the Emperor] dispatched envoys to instruct Mujian to come out.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor reached Guzang, he sent envoys ordering Mujian to surrender.

sentences.zh: 牧犍聞蠕蠕內侵於善無，幸車駕返斾，遂嬰城自守。

translations.literal: Mujian heard the Rouran were invading inward at Shanwu and hoped the imperial carriage would turn its banners in return; he then closed the city and held it himself.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that the Rouran had launched an invasion at Shanwu, Mujian hoped the Emperor would turn back—and barricaded himself inside the city.

sentences.zh: 牧犍兄子祖踰城出降，具知其情，世祖乃引諸軍進攻。

translations.literal: Mujian's elder brother's son Zu climbed over the wall and came out to surrender, fully knowing their situation; Emperor Shizu thereupon led the various armies forward in attack.
translations.idiomatic: Mujian's nephew Zu climbed over the wall to surrender, reporting everything he knew; Emperor Shizu then ordered a full assault.

sentences.zh: 牧犍兄子萬年率麾下又來降。

translations.literal: Mujian's elder brother's son Wannian, leading his subordinates, also came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Mujian's nephew Wannian also defected with his followers.

sentences.zh: 城拔，牧犍與左右文武面縛請罪，詔釋其縛。

translations.literal: When the city was taken, Mujian and his immediate civil and military officials, with faces bound, requested punishment; an edict released their bonds.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Mujian and his officials bound themselves in surrender and pleaded for mercy; the Emperor ordered their bonds cut.

sentences.zh: 徙涼州民三萬餘家于京師。

translations.literal: More than thirty thousand households of Liangzhou people were relocated to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: More than thirty thousand Liangzhou households were resettled in the capital.

sentences.zh: 初，太延中，有一父老投書於敦煌城東門，忽然不見，其書一紙八字，文曰：「涼王三十年，若七年。」

translations.literal: Earlier, during Taiyan, an old man submitted a letter at the east gate of Dunhuang city and suddenly disappeared; the letter was one sheet of eight characters, reading: "The King of Liang thirty years, if seven years."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Taiyan era, an old man left a letter at Dunhuang's east gate and vanished without a trace. The single sheet bore eight characters: "Thirty years for the King of Liang—or seven."

sentences.zh: 又於震電之所得石，丹書曰：「河西、河西三十年，破帶石，樂七年。」

translations.literal: Also from a stone obtained during thunder and lightning, cinnabar writing said: "Hexi, Hexi thirty years; when Daisi is broken, Le seven years."
translations.idiomatic: Later, during a thunderstorm, a stone was found inscribed in cinnabar: "Hexi, Hexi—thirty years; break Daisi, Le seven years.

sentences.zh: 帶石，山名，在姑臧南山祀傍，泥陷不通。

translations.literal: Daisi is a mountain name, beside a shrine south of Guzang; mud trapped [the road] and it was impassable.
translations.idiomatic: Daisi was a mountain south of Guzang, near a local shrine, blocked by mud and impassable.

sentences.zh: 牧犍征南大將軍董來曰：「祀豈有知乎！」

translations.literal: Mujian's Grand General Who Conquers the South Donglai said: "How could a shrine have knowledge!"
translations.idiomatic: Mujian's Grand General Who Conquers the South, Donglai, said, "What does a shrine know!

sentences.zh: 遂毀祀伐木，通道而行。

translations.literal: Thereupon they destroyed the shrine, felled trees, cleared a path, and passed through.
translations.idiomatic: They demolished the shrine, cut down the trees, cleared a road, and passed through.

sentences.zh: 牧犍立，果七年而滅，如其言。

translations.literal: When Mujian established [himself], indeed after seven years he was destroyed, just as the words said.
translations.idiomatic: Mujian's reign lasted exactly seven years before destruction—just as the prophecy foretold.

sentences.zh: 牧犍淫嫂李氏，兄弟三人傳嬖之。

translations.literal: Mujian fornicated with his sister-in-law Lady Li; the three brothers passed her among themselves as favorite.
translations.idiomatic: Mujian took his sister-in-law Lady Li as lover, and all three brothers shared her by turns.

sentences.zh: 李與牧犍姊共毒公主，上遣解毒醫乘傳救公主得愈。

translations.literal: Li and Mujian's elder sister together poisoned the Princess; the Emperor dispatched a detoxifying physician by relay post to save the Princess, who recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li and Mujian's sister conspired to poison the Princess; the Emperor sent a physician by urgent relay, and the Princess recovered.

sentences.zh: 上徵李氏，牧犍不遣，厚送居於酒泉，上大怒。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Lady Li; Mujian did not send her, richly escorting her to reside at Jiuquan instead; the Emperor was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor demanded Lady Li, Mujian refused to send her and instead richly escorted her to Jiuquan; the Emperor was furious.

sentences.zh: 既克，猶以妹壻待之。

translations.literal: After the conquest, [the Emperor] still treated him as a brother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Even after the conquest, the Emperor still treated him as a brother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 其母死，以王太妃禮葬焉。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he buried her with the rites for a royal consort-grandmother.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he had her buried with the honors due a royal princess-consort.

sentences.zh: 又為蒙遜置守墓三十家。

translations.literal: He also established thirty households to guard Mengxun's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: He also assigned thirty households to tend Mengxun's tomb.

sentences.zh: 改授牧犍征西大將軍、王如故。

translations.literal: [Mujian's title] was changed to appoint him Grand General Who Conquers the West; his kingship remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Mujian was reappointed Grand General Who Conquers the West, retaining his royal title.

sentences.zh: 初，官軍未入之間，牧犍使人斫開府庫，取金銀珠玉及珍奇器物，不更封閉。

translations.literal: Earlier, before the imperial army entered, Mujian had men hack open the treasury, take gold, silver, pearls, jade, and rare and wondrous objects, and not reseal it.
translations.idiomatic: Before the imperial army entered the city, Mujian had the treasury broken open and its gold, silver, gems, and treasures looted without being resealed.

sentences.zh: 小民因之入盜，巨細蕩盡。

translations.literal: The common folk thereupon entered to steal; great and small were utterly swept clean.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners rushed in to loot as well, until nothing large or small remained.

sentences.zh: 有司求賊不得。

translations.literal: The responsible offices sought the thieves but could not find them.
translations.idiomatic: Officials searched for the culprits in vain.

sentences.zh: 真君八年，其所親人及守藏者告之，上乃窮竟其事，搜其家中，悉得所藏器物。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhenjun, his intimates and treasury keepers reported it; the Emperor thereupon thoroughly investigated the matter, searched their homes, and completely recovered the hidden objects.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenjun 8, Mujian's confidants and treasury keepers came forward; the Emperor investigated thoroughly, searched their homes, and recovered all the stolen goods.

sentences.zh: 又告牧犍父子多畜毒藥，前後隱竊殺人乃有百數；

translations.literal: They also reported that Mujian and his sons stored much poison; before and after, by secret murder the victims amounted to a full hundred;
translations.idiomatic: Informants also reported that Mujian and his sons hoarded poisons and had secretly killed as many as a hundred people;

sentences.zh: 姊妹皆為左道，朋行淫佚，曾無愧顏。

translations.literal: The sisters all practiced heterodox ways, associated in licentiousness, and never showed a face of shame.
translations.idiomatic: His sisters all practiced forbidden rites and consorted in debauchery without a trace of shame.

sentences.zh: 始罽賓沙門曰曇無讖，東入鄯善，自云「能使鬼治病，令婦人多子」，與鄯善王妹曼頭陀林私通。

translations.literal: Initially a Kasmira Buddhist monk named Tan Wuchen entered east into Shanshan, claiming himself "able to make ghosts heal disease and give women many sons," and had secret relations with the Shanshan king's younger sister Mantuotuolin.
translations.idiomatic: A Buddhist monk from Kashmir named Tan Wuchen had traveled east to Shanshan, proclaiming that he could summon spirits to heal the sick and bless women with many sons. He had an affair with the Shanshan king's sister, Mantuotuolin.

sentences.zh: 發覺，亡奔涼州。

translations.literal: When discovered, he fled to Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When this was discovered, he fled to Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜寵之，號曰「聖人」。

translations.literal: Mengxun favored him and styled him "the Sage."
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun took him under his patronage and called him "the Sage."

sentences.zh: 曇無讖以男女交接之術教授婦人，蒙遜諸女、子婦皆往受法。

translations.literal: Tan Wuchen taught women the art of sexual intercourse; Mengxun's daughters and daughters-in-law all went to receive the method.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Wuchen taught women techniques of sexual union, and Mengxun's daughters and daughters-in-law all came to receive instruction.

sentences.zh: 世祖聞諸行人，言曇無讖之術，乃召曇無讖。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu heard from various travelers speak of Tan Wuchen's arts and thereupon summoned Tan Wuchen.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu heard travelers' accounts of Tan Wuchen's practices and summoned him to court.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜不遣，遂發露其事，拷訊殺之。

translations.literal: Mengxun would not send him; he thereupon exposed the affair, tortured and interrogated, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun refused to send him; instead he exposed the scandal, had Tan Wuchen tortured, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 至此，帝知之，於是賜昭儀沮渠氏死，誅其宗族，唯萬年及祖以前先降得免。

translations.literal: At this point the Emperor learned of it; thereupon he granted death to Imperial Concubine Lady Juqu, executed her clan, and only Wannian and Zu, having surrendered earlier, were spared.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor learned the full extent of it, he ordered Imperial Concubine Lady Juqu to take her own life and executed her entire clan. Only Wannian and Zu were spared, having defected earlier.

sentences.zh: 是年，人又告牧犍猶與故臣民交通謀反，詔司徒崔浩就公主第賜牧犍死。

translations.literal: That year, men again reported that Mujian still communicated with former ministers and people plotting rebellion; an edict ordered Minister of Education Cui Hao to go to the Princess's residence and grant Mujian death.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, informants reported that Mujian was still conspiring with his former subjects. An edict sent Minister of Education Cui Hao to the Princess's residence to order Mujian's death.

sentences.zh: 牧犍與主訣，良久乃自裁，葬以王禮，諡曰哀王。

translations.literal: Mujian took leave of the Princess; after a long while he then killed himself; he was buried with royal rites and given the posthumous title King Ai.
translations.idiomatic: Mujian bid farewell to the Princess and, after a long silence, took his own life. He was buried with royal honors and posthumously titled King Ai.

sentences.zh: 及公主薨，詔與牧犍合葬。

translations.literal: When the Princess died, an edict ordered joint burial with Mujian.
translations.idiomatic: When the Princess died, an edict ordered that she be buried alongside Mujian.

sentences.zh: 公主無男，有女，以國甥親寵，得襲母爵為武威公主。

translations.literal: The Princess had no sons but had a daughter; as a close favorite niece of the state, [she] was able to inherit her mother's enfeoffment as Princess Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess had no sons but a daughter, who as the Emperor's favored niece inherited her mother's title as Princess Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜子秉，字季義。

translations.literal: Mengxun's son Bing, styled Jiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun's son Bing, courtesy name Jiyi.

sentences.zh: 世祖以其父故，拜東雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu, on account of his father, appointed him Governor of Eastern Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Out of regard for his father, Emperor Shizu appointed him Governor of Eastern Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 險詖多端，真君中，遂與河東蜀薛安都謀逆。

translations.literal: Treacherous and deceitful in many ways, during Zhenjun he then joined with Shu of Hedong, Xue Andu, in plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Treacherous and scheming, he eventually conspired with Xue Andu of Shu in Hedong to rebel during the Zhenjun era.

sentences.zh: 至京師，付其兄弟扼而殺之。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital, [13] he was handed over to his brothers who strangled him and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the capital, [13] he was handed to his brothers, who strangled him.

sentences.zh: 萬年、祖並以先降，萬年拜安西將軍、張掖王，祖為廣武公。

translations.literal: Wannian and Zu both on account of earlier surrender—Wannian was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and King of Zhangye; Zu was made Duke of Guangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Wannian and Zu were rewarded for their early defection: Wannian was made General Who Pacifies the West and King of Zhangye, and Zu was enfeoffed as Duke of Guangwu.

sentences.zh: 萬年後為冀定二州刺史，復坐謀逆，與祖俱死。

translations.literal: Later Wannian served as Governor of Ji and Ding provinces; again convicted of plotting rebellion, he and Zu both died.
translations.idiomatic: Wannian later served as Governor of Ji and Ding, but was again convicted of conspiracy and executed alongside Zu.

sentences.zh: 初，牧犍之敗也，弟樂都太守安周南奔吐谷渾，世祖遣鎮南將軍奚眷討之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Mujian was defeated, his younger brother Anzhou, Administrator of Ledu, fled south to Tuyuhun; Emperor Shizu dispatched General Who Guards the South Xi Juan to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: When Mujian fell, his younger brother Anzhou, Administrator of Ledu, fled south to Tuyuhun; Emperor Shizu sent General Who Guards the South Xi Juan against him.

sentences.zh: 牧犍弟酒泉太守無諱奔晉昌，乃使弋陽公元絜守酒泉。

translations.literal: Mujian's younger brother Wujie, Administrator of Jiuquan, fled to Jinchang; [the Emperor] thereupon sent Prince of Yiyang Yuan Jie to garrison Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: Mujian's brother Wujie, Administrator of Jiuquan, fled to Jinchang; the Emperor dispatched Prince of Yiyang Yuan Jie to hold Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 真君初，無諱圍酒泉，絜輕之，出城與語，為無諱所執。

translations.literal: In early Zhenjun, Wujie besieged Jiuquan; Jie looked down on him, went out of the city to speak with him, and was seized by Wujie.
translations.idiomatic: In early Zhenjun, Wujie besieged Jiuquan; Yuan Jie underestimated him, ventured out to parley, and was captured.

sentences.zh: 絜所部相率固守，無諱仍圍之，糧盡為無諱所陷。

translations.literal: Jie's subordinates together held firm; Wujie still besieged them; when provisions were exhausted they were taken by Wujie.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jie's troops held the city, but Wujie maintained the siege until provisions ran out and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 無諱又圍張掖，不能克，退保臨松，遂還。

translations.literal: Wujie again besieged Zhangye but could not take it; he withdrew to hold Linxiang and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Wujie next besieged Zhangye but failed to capture it; he withdrew to Linxiang and returned.

sentences.zh: 世祖下詔喻之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu issued an edict to instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu issued an edict admonishing him.

sentences.zh: 時永昌王健鎮涼州，無諱使其中尉梁偉詣健，求奉酒泉，又送絜及統帥兵士于健軍。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Jian of Yongchang was garrisoning Liangzhou; Wujie sent his Central Commandant Liang Wei to visit Jian, requesting to submit Jiuquan, and also sent Jie and the commanding soldiers to Jian's army.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian of Yongchang was then commanding Liangzhou; Wujie sent his Central Commandant Liang Wei to offer submission of Jiuquan and delivered Yuan Jie and the garrison troops to Wang Jian's command.

sentences.zh: 二年春，世祖遣兼鴻臚持節策拜無諱為征西大將軍、涼州牧、酒泉王。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year, Emperor Shizu dispatched Acting Grand Master of Ceremonies bearing credentials to invest Wujie as Grand General Who Conquers the West, Governor of Liangzhou, and King of Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year, the Emperor sent an Acting Grand Master of Ceremonies with credentials to invest Wujie as Grand General Who Conquers the West, Governor of Liangzhou, and King of Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 尋以無諱復規叛逆，復遣鎮南將軍、南陽公奚眷討酒泉，克之。

translations.literal: Soon because Wujie again plotted rebellion, [the Emperor] again dispatched General Who Guards the South, Duke of Nanyang Xi Juan, to campaign against Jiuquan and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wujie was again plotting rebellion; the Emperor sent General Who Guards the South, Duke of Nanyang Xi Juan, to seize Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 無諱遂謀渡流沙，遣安周西擊鄯善。

translations.literal: Wujie thereupon planned to cross the flowing sands; he sent Anzhou west to strike Shanshan.
translations.idiomatic: Wujie then planned to flee across the desert; he sent Anzhou west to attack Shanshan.

sentences.zh: 鄯善王恐懼欲降，會魏使者勸令拒守。

translations.literal: The Shanshan king in fear wished to surrender; it happened that a Wei envoy urged him to hold and resist.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Shanshan, terrified, was about to surrender when a Wei envoy arrived and persuaded him to hold out.

sentences.zh: 安周遂與連戰，不能克，退保東城。

translations.literal: Anzhou thereupon engaged them in repeated battles but could not take them; he withdrew to hold the eastern city.
translations.idiomatic: Anzhou fought repeated engagements but could not prevail and withdrew to hold the eastern city.

sentences.zh: 三年春，鄯善王比龍西奔且末，其世子乃從安周，鄯善大亂。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year, the Shanshan king Bilong fled west to Qiemo; his heir then followed Anzhou, and Shanshan fell into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year, King Bilong of Shanshan fled west to Qiemo while his crown prince sided with Anzhou; Shanshan plunged into chaos.

sentences.zh: 無諱遂渡流沙，士卒渴死者太半，仍據鄯善。

translations.literal: Wujie thereupon crossed the flowing sands; more than half the soldiers died of thirst; he still occupied Shanshan.
translations.idiomatic: Wujie crossed the desert, losing more than half his army to thirst, but still secured Shanshan.

sentences.zh: 先是，高昌太守闞爽為李寶舅唐契所攻，聞無諱至鄯善，遣使詐降，欲令無諱與唐契相擊。

translations.literal: Earlier, Gaochang Administrator Kan Shuang was attacked by Li Bao's maternal uncle Tang Qi; hearing Wujie had reached Shanshan, he sent envoys feigning surrender, wishing to make Wujie and Tang Qi strike each other.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Kan Shuang, Administrator of Gaochang, was under attack by Tang Qi, uncle of Li Bao. Hearing that Wujie had reached Shanshan, he feigned surrender, hoping to set Wujie against Tang Qi.

sentences.zh: 無諱留安周住鄯善，從焉耆東北趣高昌。

translations.literal: Wujie left Anzhou to remain in Shanshan and, from northeast of Yanqi, pressed toward Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: Wujie left Anzhou in Shanshan and marched on Gaochang from the northeast via Yanqi.

sentences.zh: 會蠕蠕殺唐契，爽拒無諱，無諱將衞興奴詐誘爽，遂屠其城，爽奔蠕蠕。

translations.literal: It happened the Rouran killed Tang Qi; Shuang resisted Wujie; Wujie's general Wei Xingnu deceitfully lured Shuang, then massacred his city; Shuang fled to the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran killed Tang Qi, and when Kan Shuang refused to submit, Wujie's general Wei Xingnu lured him by deceit, sacked the city, and sent Shuang fleeing to the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 無諱因留高昌。

translations.literal: Wujie thereupon remained at Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: Wujie then made Gaochang his base.

sentences.zh: 五年夏，無諱病死，安周代立。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fifth year, Wujie died of illness; Anzhou succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fifth year, Wujie died of illness, and Anzhou succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 後為蠕蠕國所并。

translations.literal: Later [the realm] was annexed by the Rouran state.
translations.idiomatic: Later their realm was absorbed by the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：周德之衰，七雄競跱，咸分割神州，睥睨尊極。

translations.literal: The history minister states: When Zhou virtue declined, the seven heroes competed and contended; all divided the divine land and looked down upon the supreme throne.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: When Zhou virtue waned, the seven warring states vied for power, each carving up the realm and reaching for the throne.

sentences.zh: 至是，張寔等介在人外，地實戎墟，大爭鵄張，[14]潛懷不遜，其不知量固為甚矣。

translations.literal: By this time Zhang Shi and the others stood apart among men; the land was truly barbarian ruins; they greatly contended with owl-spread wings; [14] secretly harbored disobedience—their ignorance of measure was indeed very great.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zhang Shi and his like held only marginal ground in a land that was barely more than barbarian waste. They strutted like owls on the wing, [14] nursed secret defiance, and grossly misjudged their own strength.

sentences.zh: 蛇虺相噬，終為擒滅，宜哉。

translations.literal: Snakes and vipers devoured one another; in the end they were captured and destroyed—as they should have been.
translations.idiomatic: Serpents devouring one another—they were captured and destroyed in the end. It was only fitting.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 茂妻弟賈模兄弟謀害茂 殿本考證云：「按晉書張茂傳

translations.literal: Mao's wife's younger brother Jia Mo and his brothers plotted to harm Mao. The Palace edition textual notes say: "According to the Jin Shu biography of Zhang Mao
translations.idiomatic: Mao's wife's younger brother Jia Mo and his brothers plotted to harm Mao. The Palace edition textual notes say: "According to the Jin Shu biography of Zhang Mao

sentences.zh: 〈卷八六〉

translations.literal: 〈Volume 86〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Volume 86〉

sentences.zh: 云：『涼州大姓賈摹，寔之妻弟也。』

translations.literal: it says: 'The great clan of Liangzhou, Jia Mo, was Shi's wife's younger brother.'
translations.idiomatic: it says: 'The great Liangzhou clan of Jia Mo was Shi's wife's younger brother.'

sentences.zh: 此以為茂之妻弟，與晉書異。

translations.literal: Here it is taken as Mao's wife's younger brother, which differs from the Jin Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Here the text treats him as Mao's wife's younger brother, which differs from the Jin Shu.

sentences.zh: 又按茂傳有『手莫頭，圖涼州』之謠，則字當從『手』上『莫』。」

translations.literal: Further, according to Mao's biography there is the rhyme 'Shou Motou, plotting Liangzhou,' so the character should follow 'shou' with 'mo.'"
translations.idiomatic: Further, Mao's biography records the rhyme 'Shou Motou, plotting Liangzhou,' so the character should be 'mo' following 'shou.'"

sentences.zh: 興晉金城 諸本「興晉、金城」作「金興晉城」。

translations.literal: Xingjin and Jincheng. In the various editions "Xingjin and Jincheng" read "Jinxing Jincheng."
translations.idiomatic: Xingjin and Jincheng. The various editions read "Jinxing Jincheng" for "Xingjin and Jincheng."

sentences.zh: 按晉書卷一四地理志上作「興晉、金城」。

translations.literal: According to Jin Shu, volume 14, Geography Monograph A, it reads "Xingjin and Jincheng."
translations.idiomatic: Jin Shu, volume 14, Geography Monograph A, has "Xingjin and Jincheng."

sentences.zh: 這裏誤倒，今乙正。

translations.literal: Here the order is mistakenly reversed; it is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: The order here was reversed in error and has now been corrected.

sentences.zh: 西平公 諸本「西平」作「平西」，晉書卷八六張軌傳作「西平」。

translations.literal: Duke of Xiping. In the various editions "Xiping" reads "Pingxi"; Jin Shu, volume 86, biography of Zhang Gui, reads "Xiping."
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Xiping. The various editions read "Pingxi" for "Xiping"; Jin Shu, volume 86, biography of Zhang Gui, has "Xiping."

sentences.zh: 按自張軌封西平公之後，子孫繼位之初，自稱或受晉封都是「西平公」。

translations.literal: According to this, from the time Zhang Gui was enfeoffed as Duke of Xiping, at the beginning of each successor's accession, whether styling themselves or receiving Jin enfeoffment, all were "Duke of Xiping."
translations.idiomatic: From Zhang Gui's enfeoffment as Duke of Xiping onward, each successor at the start of his reign styled himself or received Jin investiture as "Duke of Xiping."

sentences.zh: 這裏「平西」乃誤倒，今乙正。

translations.literal: Here "Pingxi" is a mistaken reversal; it is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: "Pingxi" here is a reversed error and has now been corrected.

sentences.zh: 改年為建洪 北史卷九三「洪」作「弘」，當是魏收避魏諱改「洪」，下慕末改年永洪，北史也作「永弘」。

translations.literal: Changed the era name to Jianhong. In Beishi, volume 93, hong (grandeur) reads hong (vast); this should be Wei Shou's taboo avoidance under Wei, substituting one homophone for another; below, Mumo changed the era to Yonghong, and Beishi also reads Yonghong with the alternate character.
translations.idiomatic: Changed the era name to Jianhong. Beishi, volume 93, uses a different homophone for hong—likely Wei Shou avoiding a taboo character under Wei naming conventions. Below, Mumo later changed the era to Yonghong; Beishi likewise uses the alternate form.

sentences.zh: 不再出校記。

translations.literal: No further collation notes are given.
translations.idiomatic: No further collation notes are given.

sentences.zh: 後遣其尚書郎莫胡 北史卷九三西秦傳「莫」下有「者」字。

translations.literal: Later sent his Secretariat Gentleman Mo Hu. In Beishi, volume 93, Western Qin biography, after "Mo" there is the character "zhe."
translations.idiomatic: Later sent his Secretariat Gentleman Mo Hu. Beishi, volume 93, Western Qin biography, has the character "zhe" after "Mo."

sentences.zh: 按「莫者」是複姓，見元和姓纂卷一四、廣韵卷九鐸韵、通志氏族略，這裏當脫「者」字。

translations.literal: According to this, "Mozhe" is a compound surname, seen in Yuanhe Xingzuan, volume 14; Guangyun, volume 9, Duo rhyme; and Tongzhi, Clans Summary; here the character "zhe" must be missing.
translations.idiomatic: "Mozhe" is a compound surname attested in Yuanhe Xingzuan, volume 14; Guangyun, volume 9, Duo rhyme; and Tongzhi, Clans Summary. The character "zhe" is missing here.

sentences.zh: 殺秦州刺史胡烈於萬斛堆 諸本「萬」作「高」，晉書卷一二六禿髮烏孤載記作「萬」。

translations.literal: Killed Qinzhou Inspector Hu Lie at Wandudui. In the various editions "wan" reads "gao"; Jin Shu, volume 126, annals of Tufa Wugu, reads "wan."
translations.idiomatic: Killed Qinzhou Inspector Hu Lie at Wandudui. The various editions read "gao" for "wan"; Jin Shu, volume 126, annals of Tufa Wugu, has "wan."

sentences.zh: 按晉書卷三武帝紀泰始六年六月、卷五七胡奮傳附見胡烈都作「萬斛堆」。

translations.literal: According to Jin Shu, volume 3, Annals of Emperor Wu, sixth month of the sixth year of Taishi, and volume 57, biography of Hu Fen with appended mention of Hu Lie, all read "Wandudui."
translations.idiomatic: Jin Shu, volume 3, Annals of Emperor Wu, sixth month of the sixth year of Taishi, and volume 57, biography of Hu Fen with appended mention of Hu Lie, all have "Wandudui."

sentences.zh: 「高」乃「萬」字形近而訛，今據改。

translations.literal: "Gao" is a graphic confusion near "wan"; it is now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: "Gao" is a graphic confusion for "wan" and has now been emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 斬二千餘級 諸本無「斬」字，於文理不洽，今據晉書卷一二六補。

translations.literal: Slew more than two thousand [enemy heads]. In the various editions the character "zhan" is absent; the sense is incomplete; it is now supplemented according to Jin Shu, volume 126.
translations.idiomatic: Slew more than two thousand heads. The various editions lack the character "zhan," leaving the sense incomplete; it is now supplied from Jin Shu, volume 126.

sentences.zh: 懼為蒙遜所滅 諸本脫「為」字，於文理不洽，今據晉書卷一二六補。

translations.literal: Feared being destroyed by Mengxun. In the various editions the character "wei" is missing; the sense is incomplete; it is now supplemented according to Jin Shu, volume 126.
translations.idiomatic: Feared being destroyed by Mengxun. The various editions omit the character "wei," leaving the sense incomplete; it is now supplied from Jin Shu, volume 126.

sentences.zh: 祖太 按晉書卷八七涼武昭王傳、北史卷一００自序、御覽卷一二四

translations.literal: Zu Tai. According to Jin Shu, volume 87, biography of the Martial and Illustrious King of Liang; Beishi, volume 100, author's preface; and Yulan, volume 124
translations.idiomatic: Zu Tai. According to Jin Shu, volume 87, biography of the Martial and Illustrious King of Liang; Beishi, volume 100, author's preface; and Yulan, volume 124

sentences.zh: 〈六０一頁〉

translations.literal: 〈Page 601〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Page 601〉

sentences.zh: 引十六國春秋前涼錄都作「弇」，御覽且注「音掩」。

translations.literal: The Former Liang Record in the Sixteen Kingdoms Spring and Autumn consistently gives Yan, and the Imperial Digest glosses the pronunciation as yan.
translations.idiomatic: The Former Liang Record in the Sixteen Kingdoms Spring and Autumn consistently gives Yan, and the Imperial Digest glosses the pronunciation as yan.

sentences.zh: 疑「太」字訛。

translations.literal: The character tai is probably a scribal error.
translations.idiomatic: The character tai is probably a scribal error.

sentences.zh: 大破沮渠蒙遜於鮮支澗 諸本「鮮」作「解」。

translations.literal: He routed Juqu Mengxun at Xianzhi Stream; various editions read jie for xian.
translations.idiomatic: He routed Juqu Mengxun at Xianzhi Stream; various editions read jie for xian.

sentences.zh: 按晉書卷一０安帝紀義熙十三年夏作「鮮」，卷一二九沮渠蒙遜載記作「解」。

translations.literal: Jin Shu, volume 10 (Annals of Emperor An), summer of Yixi 13, has xian; volume 129 (Record of Juqu Mengxun) has jie.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Shu, volume 10 (Annals of Emperor An), summer of Yixi 13, has xian; volume 129 (Record of Juqu Mengxun) has jie.

sentences.zh: 檢宋書卷九八沮渠蒙遜傳作「西」，「鮮」「西」音近，知晉書載記及此傳「解」並是「鮮」字形訛，今據晉書安帝紀改。

translations.literal: Song Shu, volume 98, reads xi; since xian and xi are phonetically close, jie in the Jin Shu record and this biography are both corrupt forms of xian—the text is emended to match the Jin Shu Annals of Emperor An.
translations.idiomatic: Song Shu, volume 98, reads xi; since xian and xi are phonetically close, jie in the Jin Shu record and this biography are both corrupt forms of xian—the text is emended to match the Jin Shu Annals of Emperor An.

sentences.zh: 請為安西太守 晉書卷一二九沮渠蒙遜載記「安西」作「西安」。

translations.literal: He requested appointment as governor of Anxi; Jin Shu, volume 129, reads Xi'an instead of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: He requested appointment as governor of Anxi; Jin Shu, volume 129, reads Xi'an instead of Anxi.

sentences.zh: 按載記上文稱「業作西安城，以其將臧莫孩為太守」，晉書卷一二二呂光載記見「光西安太守石元良」。

translations.literal: According to the record above: 'Ye built Xi'an city and made his general Zang Mohai its governor'; Jin Shu, volume 122, Record of Lü Guang, mentions 'Lü Guang's Governor of Xi'an Shi Yuanliang.'
translations.idiomatic: The record above states that Ye built Xi'an city and appointed his general Zang Mohai governor; Jin Shu, volume 122, mentions Lü Guang's governor of Xi'an, Shi Yuanliang.

sentences.zh: 當時呂光有西安郡，段業既反光自立，別築城以立郡，亦名「西安」。

translations.literal: At that time Lü Guang held the commandery of Xi'an; after Duan Ye rebelled against Guang and declared himself ruler, he built a separate city to establish a commandery, also named Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang then held Xi'an commandery; when Duan Ye broke away and declared independence, he founded a new city as a commandery seat, likewise called Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 「安西」不見載記，當是誤倒。

translations.literal: Anxi does not occur in the record and is presumably a transposed reading.
translations.idiomatic: Anxi does not occur in the record and is presumably a transposed reading.

sentences.zh: 憑援谷軍 「谷軍」不可解，「谷」字當訛。

translations.literal: He relied on the Gujun forces; the term gujun is unintelligible and the character gu is probably corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: He relied on the Gujun forces; the term gujun is unintelligible and the character gu is probably corrupt.

sentences.zh: 至京師 北史卷九三北涼傳「至」上有「召」字。

translations.literal: He arrived at the capital; Beishi, volume 93, has the character zhao ('summoned') before zhi ('arrived').
translations.idiomatic: He arrived at the capital; Beishi, volume 93, has the character zhao ('summoned') before zhi ('arrived').

sentences.zh: 按此字不宜省，當是脫文。

translations.literal: This character should not be omitted; it is likely a lacuna in the text.
translations.idiomatic: This character ought not to be omitted; the text has probably dropped it.

sentences.zh: 大爭鵄張 「大爭」疑是「犬爭」之訛。

translations.literal: Great strife, owls abroad—the reading da zheng is probably a corruption of quan zheng ('dogs at strife').
translations.idiomatic: Great strife, owls abroad—the reading da zheng is probably a corruption of quan zheng ('dogs at strife').
